countries.body: TurnTable Certification System of Nigeria (TCSN) — TurnTable Charts / TurnTable Media, Data and Analytics
countries.unitDefinition: Sales + streaming equivalents, with a fixed stream-to-unit ratio that DIFFERS between formats. TCSN's own wording, singles: "The certification system is based on on-demand streaming and digital downloads. For on-demand streaming, paid streams weigh higher than ad-supported streams." / "At the moment, the certification for single is based on audio streaming and digital downloads. 1 unit = 150 streams". Albums: "At the moment, the certification for album is based on audio streaming and digital downloads. A title is classified as an 'album' if it has more than three singles and/or surpasses a 15-minute runtime. 1 unit = 1500 streams". So a Platinum single = 100,000 units = 15,000,000 on-demand streams, which the body itself states in its first-Platinum announcement: BNXN's "Kilometer (Remix)" got the plaque "for surpassing 15 million on-demand streams in Nigeria". The body says paid streams weigh higher than ad-supported ones but publishes NO separate per-tier weighting table for certification; the "methodology behind the weighing of streams" link on the certification announcement points to its CHART methodology (https://www.turntablecharts.com/news/480, 7 Mar 2023: paid/Apple Music 1.0 point per play, freemium/Spotify 0.75, YouTube ad-supported video 0.66, other ad-supported 0.5), which is the Nigeria Top 100 chart formula, not a published certification conversion table. Only streams inside Nigeria count: the application page requires "streaming & digital download report (for streams within Nigeria only)".
countries.multiplierRule: Multi-Platinum = literally N x the Platinum threshold. The certification application page lists the levels an applicant may request as "Silver, Gold, Platinum or Multi-Platinum" (turntablecharts.com/certification, Application tab). The body's own arithmetic, in a 10 Mar 2026-era feature dated 2 Mar 2026: CKay's "Body (danz)" "is certified 2X Platinum, moving over 200,000 singles units in the country since release" (https://www.turntablecharts.com/news/2084) — i.e. 2x = 2 x 100,000 single units. The same article gives the song "over 33 million on-demand streams", consistent with the 150 streams = 1 unit ratio still being in force in 2026. TCSN publishes no ceiling; its live register currently tops out at 8x Platinum ("Lonely At The Top", Asake). Note: no body statement was found defining multi-platinum for ALBUMS specifically; by the same rule it would be N x 50,000 album units, but the body has not written that down.
countries.diamondRule: There is NO Diamond tier at TCSN. The launch announcement defines the programme as "The awards (silver, gold and platinum)" and its Standards section lists only Silver / Gold / Platinum for both singles and albums. The application instructions likewise offer only "Silver, Gold, Platinum or Multi-Platinum". The site's own plaque-icon map in the certification page bundle contains three artworks only (silver, gold, platinum). The public register serves nothing above Platinum_8. So above Platinum the only award is Nx Platinum; Diamond is not a threshold TCSN awards, and any "Diamond" string on the certification page is an artist/title name (Diamond Jimma, "Diamonds" by Wizkid, Blaq Diamond), not a tier.
countries.changedSince2015: No change on record — but note the system is younger than the window. TCSN did not exist before 2023: TurnTable announced the certification arm and published these standards on 18 FEBRUARY 2023, with "The official application process for the certification will launch on Monday, February 20, 2023." The body has published no revision to the unit ratios or the Silver/Gold/Platinum thresholds since, and its own March 2026 reporting (2X Platinum = over 200,000 singles units, ~33m streams) is arithmetically consistent with the Feb-2023 numbers, so the 2023 standards are the current ones as of 10 Sep 2026. Practical consequence for plaques dated 2018-2026: TCSN states "All TCSN certification awards date back to beginning of digital era (iTunes) in Nigeria", i.e. pre-2023 consumption is counted retroactively against these same thresholds, so a 2018-era Nigerian plaque is still priced on the 2023 standard. Every entry in the current public register carries a certified date of Feb 6, 2026 — that is a register/batch refresh stamp, NOT evidence of a threshold change; nothing on the body's site announces new standards in 2026.
countries.notes:
Where the numbers actually live: the live /certification page publishes NO thresholds at all — it is a register (tabs: Eligible Songs / Application / Display) plus an application procedure. The only place TurnTable itself states the numbers is its two Feb 18 2023 announcements on its own site: news/751 ("TurnTable Launches Certification System Under New Arm, TCSN") and news/753 (the BNXN first-Platinum story), which carry an identical Standards section. Both were read in full (raw HTML fetched, not a summary).

Album definition is the body's own: "more than three singles and/or surpasses a 15-minute runtime". No separate EP, video, or "streaming single" categories exist; the register's only format values are Single and Album (all 500 rows currently served are Singles).

Certification is REQUEST-BASED, not automatic: requests go to tcsn@turntablecharts.com with a completed Excel request sheet, a streaming/digital-download report for Nigeria only, and a product one-sheet (UPC/ISRC, runtime, credits); "Kindly select the highest certification level you're requesting for; Silver, Gold, Platinum or Multi-Platinum." Absence of a title from the register therefore proves nothing about eligibility — only that nobody applied or the plaque has not been claimed.

Register mechanics relevant to pricing 668 plaques: the public register is a Next.js SSG page whose embedded JSON caps at exactly 500 entries (milestone distribution served today: Platinum_1 268, Platinum_2 89, Platinum_3 51, Gold_1 44, Platinum_4 33, Platinum_5 8, Platinum_6 4, Platinum_7 2, Platinum_8 1). It serves ZERO Silver rows and zero Albums at present — that is the 500-row cap and claim state, not proof that Silver is not a tier; Silver is explicitly a tier in the body's own standards.

Secondary sources contradict the body on the album line: several summaries (and search snippets) mix the album ratio (1 unit = 1500 streams) with the SINGLES thresholds, or quote album thresholds as if they were singles. The body's own text keeps them separate, and the figures reported here are the body's.
countries.sourceQuote: Standards — Singles: "At the moment, the certification for single is based on audio streaming and digital downloads. 1 unit = 150 streams. 1. Silver: 25,000 units 2. Gold: 50,000 units 3. Platinum: 100,000 units". Album: "At the moment, the certification for album is based on audio streaming and digital downloads. A title is classified as an 'album' if it has more than three singles and/or surpasses a 15-minute runtime. 1 unit = 1500 streams. 1. Silver: 12,500 units 2. Gold: 25,000 units 3. Platinum: 50,000 units". Programme scope: "The awards (silver, gold and platinum) are earned by artistes who have met certain standards and milestones." (turntablecharts.com/news/751, 18 February 2023; identical Standards section at /news/753). Multiplier evidence, body's own words: "It is certified 2X Platinum, moving over 200,000 singles units in the country since release." (turntablecharts.com/news/2084, 2 March 2026). Application levels: "Kindly select the highest certification level you're requesting for; Silver, Gold, Platinum or Multi-Platinum." (turntablecharts.com/certification, Application tab).

verdict.reproducedFrom: I found the page independently (web search for the TCSN certification standards led to turntablecharts.com/news/751), then read the RAW HTML with curl rather than trusting any summarizer, because search-engine summaries and Wikipedia visibly conflate the single and album rows on this body. PRIMARY — https://www.turntablecharts.com/news/751 "TurnTable Launches Certification System Under New Arm, TCSN", dated FEBRUARY 18, 2023, footer "TurnTable Charts is part of TurnTable Media, Data and Analytics. (c)TMDA 2026". This is the body's own site. Raw text, verbatim: "TurnTable is pleased to announce the launch of a certification system... The awards (silver, gold and platinum) are earned by artistes who have met certain standards and milestones." Background: "The certification system is based on on-demand streaming and digital downloads. For on-demand streaming, paid streams weigh higher than ad-supported streams. You can read more on methodology behind the weighing of streams here" Standards / Singles: "At the moment, the certification for single is based on audio streaming and digital downloads. 1 unit = 150 streams / 1. Silver: 25,000 units / 2. Gold: 50,000 units / 3. Platinum: 100,000 units" Standards / Album: "At the moment, the certification for album is based on audio streaming and digital downloads. A title is classified as an 'album' if it has more than three singles and/or surpasses a 15-minute runtime. 1 unit = 1500 streams / 1. Silver: 12,500 units / 2. Gold: 25,000 units / 3. Platinum: 50,000 units" The word "diamond" does not appear anywhere on the page (grep -io diamond returned zero hits). Only three tiers are named. So, read straight off the body's page: single 25,000 / 50,000 / 100,000, Diamond none; album 12,500 / 25,000 / 50,000, Diamond none. Every figure in the claim matches, and the single/album split is NOT conflated — the two ratios (150 vs 1500) and the two threshold ladders sit under separate headings. CORROBORATION 1 — the "here" link: grep of the raw HTML shows here. I fetched it: "Methodology and Policies for the TurnTable Nigeria Top 100", by Ayomide Oriowo, MARCH 7, 2023 — verbatim: "Paid-streams will be weighted as one point (1.0) per play value, freemium streams will be weighted as 0.75 point per play, ad-supported video streams from YouTube will be weighted 0.66 point per play while ad-supported streams will be weighted 0.5 point per play." It also says "Streaming will account for 50% of the chart, airplay will account for the other 50%". Confirms the claim's point exactly: this is the Nigeria Top 100 CHART formula (it even includes airplay, which certification does not), not a published certification conversion table. TCSN publishes no per-tier certification weighting table. CORROBORATION 2 — https://www.turntablecharts.com/news/753 "BNXN fka Buju Makes History With The First 'Platinum' Certified-Single in Modern Era of Nigerian Music", FEBRUARY 18, 2023: "The artiste receives the first platinum plaque for his hit single 'Kilometer (Remix)' featuring Zinoleesky - for surpassing 15 million on-demand streams in Nigeria." 100,000 units x 150 streams = 15,000,000. The body's own arithmetic reproduces. This page also republishes the identical Standards block verbatim, so it is a second independent primary citation for the same numbers. CORROBORATION 3 — https://www.turntablecharts.com/news/2084 is "Executive of the Week - Joseph Salubi", dated MARCH 2, 2026: "The song has over 33 million on-demand streams... It is certified 2X Platinum, moving over 200,000 singles units in the country since release." 33,000,000 / 150 = 220,000 units, i.e. over 200,000 = 2 x 100,000. Confirms both the multiplier rule (Nx Platinum = N x threshold) and that the 150:1 single ratio is still in force in 2026. CORROBORATION 4 — https://www.turntablecharts.com/certification, Application tab (client-rendered; I clicked it in the browser): "Kindly select the highest certification level you're requesting for; Silver, Gold, Platinum or Multi-Platinum." and "A supporting documentation is required, detailing streaming & digital download report (for streams within Nigeria only)." Both quoted strings in the claim are exact. Also on that tab: "An artiste's certification milestone represents on-demand streams (and digital downloads)" and "Note: All TCSN certification awards date back to beginning of digital era (iTunes) in Nigeria." CORROBORATION 5 — the live register on the same page: top row is "8xPLATINUM / Lonely At The Top / Asake / Single / Feb 6, 2026", exactly as claimed. The embedded JSON's milestone enum across the served rows is Platinum_1 (268), Platinum_2 (89), Platinum_3 (51), Gold_1 (44), Platinum_4 (33), Platinum_5 (8), Platinum_6 (4), Platinum_7 (2), Platinum_8 (1) — no Diamond tier, no ceiling declared. All 12 "Diamond" strings on that page are artist/title names (Diamond Jimma, "Diamonds (Wizkid)", Blaq Diamond), not a tier — I checked each in context specifically to avoid a false Diamond reading. I searched the body's own site for any later revision of the standards and found none; news/751 remains the live statement.
verdict.corrections:
No numeric correction. Every figure, both ratios, the tier set, the multiplier rule and all four quoted strings reproduce exactly off the body's own pages. Three non-numeric notes for the record:

1. "Sales + streaming equivalents" is slightly loose. TCSN never says "sales" — the wording is "on-demand streaming and digital downloads", and the application page adds "All TCSN certification awards date back to beginning of digital era (iTunes) in Nigeria." So the sales leg is digital downloads only; no physical sales component exists. Worth phrasing as "digital downloads + streaming equivalents".

2. The claim calls news/2084 "a 10 Mar 2026-era feature dated 2 Mar 2026". The article is dated March 2, 2026 and is titled "Executive of the Week - Joseph Salubi" (a CKay-manager interview, not a certification feature). The "10 Mar 2026-era" qualifier is unsupported and should be dropped; cite it as 2 Mar 2026.

3. Provenance strengthening, not a correction: news/751 is dated 18 Feb 2023, and the identical Standards block is republished verbatim on news/753 (same date). Citing both makes the threshold claim robust to a single URL going stale.

Trap flagged for whoever publishes this: Wikipedia's TCSN article and every search-engine summary I pulled state that SINGLES are "1 unit = 1500 streams" with 12,500/25,000/50,000 thresholds — i.e. they paste the ALBUM row under the singles heading. That is the exact conflation this check is meant to catch. The claim under test does not make that error; do not "correct" it toward those secondary sources.

Also correctly caveated by the claim and confirmed by me: TCSN has published no multi-platinum definition for ALBUMS. The 2X example (CKay) is a single. N x 50,000 album units is an inference, not a body statement, and should not be presented as sourced.

countries.body: BPI — British Phonographic Industry (BRIT Certified Awards)
countries.unitDefinition: Sales + streams combined into 'units'. BPI publishes NO conversion ratio of its own — it delegates the calculation entirely to the Official Charts Company. Its exact words: "When the release in question has reached the appropriate level of sales as measured by the Official Charts Company, titles are now 'automatically certified' by the BPI. Streams now count towards both album and singles certifications and are measured as per the chart eligibility rules set out by the Official Charts Company." No premium/ad-supported split, no X:1 figure, and no album-stream formula appears anywhere on the BPI's own pages. Any specific ratio (e.g. 100:1 or 1,000:1) would have to come from the OCC, which is not the certifying body — so no ratio is reported here.
countries.multiplierRule: Literally N times the Platinum threshold. The table row reads "Multi-Platinum — Multiples of 600k" (singles) and "Multiples of 300k" (albums). BPI's own worked example: "Recordings can also attain Multiple certification status – for example, an album that has achieved 3 million chart sales is denoted as having gone 10x Platinum" (3,000,000 / 300,000 = 10). The BPI's own award-search filter enumerates 1x Platinum through 26x Platinum, so a 19x award is simply 19 x 600,000 = 11,400,000 units for a single, or 19 x 300,000 = 5,700,000 for an album.
countries.diamondRule: There is NO Diamond tier at the BPI. The published tier list is Silver, Gold, Platinum, Multi-Platinum only, and the body's own award-search facet lists exactly: Silver, Gold, Platinum, Multi-Platinum, 1x–26x Platinum. Nothing above Platinum is called Diamond. The only extra honour is BRIT Billion (1 billion career UK streams, launched May 2023), which is an artist career award, not a release certification — it does not attach to a single or album.
countries.changedSince2015: No threshold VALUE has changed — the BPI publishes only one set of numbers and states no prior values anywhere. The changes it does record are to what counts and to branding, not to the levels: audio streaming folded into singles certification from 2014 and into albums from 2015; April 2018 the scheme was renamed from BPI Awards to BRIT Certified Awards, "with eligibility for video streams added for singles shortly afterwards"; May 2023 the BRIT Billion career award launched. Verbatim: "Since 2014 (Singles) and 2015 (Albums) the programme has reflected consumption through audio streaming and in April 2018 the certifications were rebranded from the BPI Awards to the BRIT Certified Awards, with eligibility for video streams added for singles shortly afterwards." So the 60k/100k/300k album and 200k/400k/600k single levels apply unchanged across the whole 2018–2026 span of plaques being priced.
countries.sourceQuote: Award Thresholds — "When the release in question has reached the appropriate level of sales as measured by the Official Charts Company, titles are now 'automatically certified' by the BPI. Streams now count towards both album and singles certifications and are measured as per the chart eligibility rules set out by the Official Charts Company." || Singles / Units: Silver 200k; Gold 400k; Platinum 600k; Multi-Platinum Multiples of 600k. || Albums / Units: Silver 60k; Gold 100k; Platinum 300k; Multi-Platinum Multiples of 300k. || Music DVDs / Units: Gold 25k; Platinum 50k; Multi-Platinum Multiples of 50k. || Career totals / Units: BRIT Billion 1 Billion. || "Recordings can also attain Multiple certification status – for example, an album that has achieved 3 million chart sales is denoted as having gone 10x Platinum."
countries.notes: HOW IT WAS READ: www.bpi.co.uk/brit-certified/award-levels and /certification-levels are dead (404 / Hivebrite shell) — the live BPI site is a Hivebrite community platform whose certification content lives in an iframe. The page www.bpi.co.uk/page/certified-awards embeds <iframe id="awards-frame" src="https://certified-awards.bpi.co.uk/">. certified-awards.bpi.co.uk is the BPI's OWN subdomain, and https://certified-awards.bpi.co.uk/about serves the Award Thresholds tables server-side. That is the page read and quoted. THIRD FORMAT: Music DVDs are a distinct category — Gold 25,000, Platinum 50,000, Multi-Platinum multiples of 50,000, no Silver tier for DVDs. No EP category: EPs are certified under one of the existing headings, and the body's format facet lists only Album, Music DVDs, Single. VIDEO STREAMS count toward singles (added shortly after April 2018), audio streams toward both. The 'units' word is BPI's own; it does not distinguish sales from stream-equivalents in its tables. BRIT Billion is career-level and should never be mapped onto a release. The body reports thresholds in thousands ('200k'), so the integers above are the literal expansion of its own shorthand.

verdict.reproducedFrom:
Primary source read: https://certified-awards.bpi.co.uk/about — the BPI's own BRIT Certified Awards site (subdomain of bpi.co.uk, the certifying body). I found it independently by searching for BPI/BRIT Certified award levels; www.bpi.co.uk/page/certified-awards is only a JS shell that points to this same site, and www.bpi.co.uk/brit-certified/ returns 404.

Under the heading "Certification Levels / Award Thresholds" the page states verbatim: "When the release in question has reached the appropriate level of sales as measured by the Official Charts Company, titles are now 'automatically certified' by the BPI. Streams now count towards both album and singles certifications and are measured as per the chart eligibility rules set out by the Official Charts Company."

It then gives two separate tables, headed "Singles | Units" and "Albums | Units":

Singles — Silver 200k; Gold 400k; Platinum 600k; Multi-Platinum "Multiples of 600k".
Albums — Silver 60k; Gold 100k; Platinum 300k; Multi-Platinum "Multiples of 300k".

Two further tables follow that are outside the single/album scope: "Music DVDs" (Gold 25k, Platinum 50k, Multi-Platinum multiples of 50k) and "Career totals" (BRIT Billion, 1 Billion).

Earlier on the same page, under "BRIT Certified Award Levels": "Silver, Gold and Platinum levels of success are measured by the awards scheme. Recordings can also attain Multiple certification status – for example, an album that has achieved 3 million chart sales is denoted as having gone 10x Platinum. Since 2014 (Singles) and 2015 (Albums) the programme has reflected consumption through audio streaming…"

Adversarial checks I ran on the raw HTML rather than a rendered summary:
- grep for "Diamond" across the about page and the site homepage: zero hits. The BPI genuinely has no Diamond tier, so Diamond = null is correct for both singles and albums.
- grep for any conversion ratio ("100:1", "1,000:1", "streams =", "streams equal"): zero hits. The page publishes no ratio of its own and defers entirely to the OCC's chart-eligibility rules, exactly as the claim states.
- grep of the certified-awards.bpi.co.uk homepage award-search filter: it enumerates 1x Platinum through 26x Platinum (all 26 present, no gaps), confirming the claim's statement about the filter and supporting the plain N-times-Platinum reading.
- Multiplier arithmetic against BPI's own worked example: 3,000,000 / 300,000 = 10, matching "10x Platinum". So 19x = 19 × 600,000 = 11,400,000 units (single) and 19 × 300,000 = 5,700,000 units (album), as claimed.
- Single/album split is not conflated: the page presents them as two distinct tables with distinct numbers, and the claim reproduces each to the correct side.
verdict.corrections:
No corrections — every figure in the claim matches the BPI's own page exactly (singles 200k/400k/600k, albums 60k/100k/300k, no Diamond, multi-platinum as literal multiples of the Platinum threshold), and both quoted passages are verbatim.

Two non-contradicting notes for whoever consumes this, neither of which changes a claimed value:

1. Completeness, not error: the same threshold section also carries a "Music DVDs" table (Gold 25k, Platinum 50k, Multi-Platinum multiples of 50k) and a "Career totals" row (BRIT Billion = 1 Billion career UK streams, calculated by the Official Charts Company). These fall outside the single/album schema, so their absence from the claim is correct scoping, not an omission of a single/album tier.

2. A historic tier the current page does NOT carry: BPI's April 2018 relaunch press coverage described a "Breakthrough" album certification at 30,000 units. It does not appear in the live Award Thresholds table on certified-awards.bpi.co.uk/about. Do not add it to the UK ladder on the strength of the 2018 press release — the body's current page is the authority, and it lists only Silver/Gold/Platinum/Multi-Platinum for albums.

One caveat on the ratio field, which I agree with as written but want stated precisely: the claim's assertion is negative ("BPI publishes no ratio"), and I verified that by full-text grep of the BPI's own about page and homepage. That is as strong as a negative can be made from the body's own site, but it is not proof that no ratio exists anywhere in BPI-adjacent material — it is proof that the certifying body does not publish one, which is the correct thing to report.

countries.body: Music Canada (Gold & Platinum Certification Program)
countries.unitDefinition: Sales + stream equivalents, with DIFFERENT ratios for singles and albums, and a premium/ad-supported split on singles. Singles formula, verbatim: "Digital & Physical Single Sales + On-Demand Audio and Video Stream Equivalents = Total Units for Single Award Certification"; "Digital and physical single sales count as 1 unit towards Single Award Certifications."; "160 eligible Premium On-Demand Audio and/or Video streams count as 1 unit towards Single Award Certifications (i.e., 160:1)."; "240 eligible Ad-Supported On-Demand Audio and/or Video streams count as 1 unit towards Single Award Certifications (i.e., 240:1)." Albums formula, verbatim: "Digital & Physical Album Sales + TEA (Track Equivalent Album) + SEA (Stream Equivalent Album) = Total Units for Album Award Certification"; "TEA: 10 track downloads = 1 unit toward Certification."; "SEA: 1500 on-demand audio streams = 1 unit toward Certification." Note the asymmetry: video streams count toward SINGLES only; the album SEA rule says "on-demand audio streams" and excludes video. Video streams count only from 1 January 2020: "On-demand official video streams within Canada from an Approved DSP, occurring after January 1, 2020."
countries.multiplierRule: Literally N times the Platinum threshold of 80,000, and Music Canada publishes the whole ladder rather than a formula. FAQ wording: "Multi-Platinum: 160,000 Units (increments of 80,000 thereafter)". The Certification Definitions table names each step: Double Platinum 160,000; Triple Platinum 240,000; Quadruple Platinum 320,000; Quintuple Platinum 400,000; 6x Platinum 480,000; 7x Platinum 560,000; 8x Platinum 640,000; 9x Platinum 720,000 — identical for Single and for Album released after 1 May 2008. CAUTION for a site holding awards up to 19x: Music Canada's published ladder STOPS at 9x Platinum and then jumps to Diamond (10x-equivalent), Double Diamond and Triple Diamond. It names no 10x–19x Platinum tier. By the '"increments of 80,000 thereafter" rule a 19x-equivalent would be 1,520,000 units, but the body does not itself label any award '19x Platinum', so treat Canadian awards above 9x as Diamond-family naming.
countries.diamondRule: Diamond is a NAMED, published tier that is numerically exactly 10x Platinum. Singles and post-May-2008 albums: Diamond 800,000 units (= 10 x 80,000); Double Diamond 1,600,000; Triple Diamond 2,400,000. For albums released before 1 May 2008 the Diamond level is 1,000,000 (= 10 x the old 100,000 Platinum), Double Diamond 2,000,000, Triple Diamond 3,000,000. Canada does award Diamond routinely — it is not decorative, and it replaces what would otherwise be called 10x Platinum.
countries.changedSince2015: No threshold VALUE has moved since 2015 — the 40,000 / 80,000 / 800,000 levels stand. What changed is what counts, and the body dates each change. September 2016: the Single Award was created — "In September 2016, Music Canada launched the new Single Award, which combines on-demand streams with digital download and physical single sales"; the same page dates the retirement of the categories it replaced as "The Digital Download and CD Single categories were retired on September 12, 2016, and units sold are eligible under the Single Award guidelines" (the FAQ page says September 16, 2016 for the same event — the body contradicts itself by four days). July 2017: albums became stream-inclusive — "In July 2017, Music Canada updated the Album Award guidelines to include Track Equivalent Album (TEA) and Stream Equivalent Album (SEA) units toward Certification." 1 January 2020: video streams became eligible. 1 April 2021: "the certification categories for Ringtone and Music DVD have been retired." The one PRIOR SET OF VALUES the body publishes is older than 2015 and is still in force for older records: albums released BEFORE 1 May 2008 use Gold 50,000 / Platinum 100,000 / Double Platinum 200,000 / ... / Diamond 1,000,000. Every plaque in the 2018–2026 window uses the post-2008 column.
countries.sourceQuote: Certification Criteria (Definitions) — "Single Awards: Music Canada recognizes the following Single Award tiers: Gold: 40,000 Units; Platinum: 80,000 Units; Multi-Platinum: 160,000 Units (increments of 80,000 thereafter); Diamond: 800,000 Units" || "Album Awards: Music Canada recognizes the following Album Award tiers: Gold: 40,000 Units; Platinum: 80,000 Units; Multi-Platinum: 160,000 Units (increments of 80,000 thereafter); Diamond: 800,000 Units. *Note that different tiers are applicable to albums released before May 1, 2008." || Certification Definitions table (Single / Album after May 1 2008 / Album before May 1 2008): Gold 40,000 / 40,000 / 50,000; Platinum 80,000 / 80,000 / 100,000; Double Platinum 160,000 / 160,000 / 200,000; Triple Platinum 240,000 / 240,000 / 300,000; Quadruple Platinum 320,000 / 320,000 / 400,000; Quintuple Platinum 400,000 / 400,000 / 500,000; 6x Platinum 480,000 / 480,000 / 600,000; 7x Platinum 560,000 / 560,000 / 700,000; 8x Platinum 640,000 / 640,000 / 800,000; 9x Platinum 720,000 / 720,000 / 900,000; Diamond 800,000 / 800,000 / 1,000,000; Double Diamond 1,600,000 / 1,600,000 / 2,000,000; Triple Diamond 2,400,000 / 2,400,000 / 3,000,000. || "* 160 eligible Premium On-Demand Audio and/or Video streams count as 1 unit towards Single Award Certifications (i.e., 160:1) * 240 eligible Ad-Supported On-Demand Audio and/or Video streams count as 1 unit towards Single Award Certifications (i.e., 240:1) ** Track Equivalent Album (TEA): 10 tracks sales = 1 unit towards Album certification *** Stream Equivalent Album (SEA): 1500 on-demand audio streams of a track = 1 unit towards Album certification"
countries.notes: NO SILVER TIER — Music Canada's published ladder begins at Gold. Singles and albums share IDENTICAL unit thresholds (40k/80k/800k) for anything released after 1 May 2008; the split is not albums-vs-singles but old-albums-vs-everything-else. HOW IT WAS READ: https://musiccanada.com/gold-platinum/ carries no numbers; the values live on two of the body's own pages, https://musiccanada.com/gold-platinum/faq/ (prose criteria + formulas) and https://musiccanada.com/certification/ (the full Certification Definitions ladder). Both read directly, both agree on every number. OTHER CATEGORIES, all retired but historically awarded: Music DVD (Gold 5,000 / Platinum 10,000 / Diamond 100,000) and Ringtone (Gold 20,000 / Platinum 40,000 / Diamond 400,000), both retired 1 April 2021; Digital Download (Gold 40,000 / Platinum 80,000 / Diamond 800,000) and CD Single (Gold 5,000 / Platinum 10,000 / Diamond 100,000), both retired 12 September 2016. A pre-Sept-2016 Canadian plaque may therefore be a 'Digital Download' award, not a 'Single' award — same numbers, different category. No EP category exists. DOUBLE-COUNTING IS EXPLICITLY ALLOWED: "Individual track sales and streaming data can be put forward for both a Single Award and Album Award Certification." Certification is APPLICATION-BASED, not automatic (unlike the BPI): "To be Certified, the rights holder (the artist or label) must submit an application through Music Canada's Gold & Platinum online portal" — so absence of a Canadian certification is not evidence a threshold was not met. Physical sales are counted on net shipments, not consumer sales. One internal inconsistency to be aware of: the FAQ dates the Digital Download / CD Single retirement to September 16, 2016 while the Certification Definitions page says September 12, 2016.

I found the pages myself before reading the claim's numbers, and pulled raw HTML with curl (not just a summarizer) so I could read the table cells directly.

PRIMARY: https://musiccanada.com/certification/ (HTTP 200, no redirect, "Certification Definitions", © 2026 Music Canada). This is Music Canada's own site — Music Canada is the CA certifying body. The page publishes a full three-column ladder (Single | Album released after May 1 2008 | Album released before May 1 2008), read off verbatim:
  Gold 40,000 | 40,000 | 50,000
  Platinum 80,000 | 80,000 | 100,000
  Double Platinum 160,000 | 160,000 | 200,000
  Triple Platinum 240,000 | 240,000 | 300,000
  Quadruple Platinum 320,000 | 320,000 | 400,000
  Quintuple Platinum 400,000 | 400,000 | 500,000
  6x Platinum 480,000 | 480,000 | 600,000
  7x Platinum 560,000 | 560,000 | 700,000
  8x Platinum 640,000 | 640,000 | 800,000
  9x Platinum 720,000 | 720,000 | 900,000
  Diamond 800,000 | 800,000 | 1,000,000
  Double Diamond 1,600,000 | 1,600,000 | 2,000,000
  Triple Diamond 2,400,000 | 2,400,000 | 3,000,000
Column headers: Single = "Digital Downloads / Streams* / Physical Singles"; Album = "Physical / Digital / TEA** / SEA***". Footnotes verbatim: "* 160 eligible Premium On-Demand Audio and/or Video streams count as 1 unit towards Single Award Certifications (i.e., 160:1)"; "* 240 eligible Ad-Supported On-Demand Audio and/or Video streams count as 1 unit towards Single Award Certifications (i.e., 240:1)"; "** Track Equivalent Album (TEA): 10 tracks sales = 1 unit towards Album certification"; "*** Stream Equivalent Album (SEA): 1500 on-demand audio streams of a track = 1 unit towards Album certification". No Silver tier appears anywhere on the page.

SECONDARY: https://musiccanada.com/gold-platinum/faq/ ("Gold & Platinum FAQ"). Under "Certification Criteria (Definitions)" it states, verbatim: Single Award tiers "Gold: 40,000 Units / Platinum: 80,000 Units / Multi-Platinum: 160,000 Units (increments of 80,000 thereafter) / Diamond: 800,000 Units", then "Digital & Physical Single Sales + On-Demand Audio and Video Stream Equivalents = Total Units for Single Award Certification", "Digital and physical single sales count as 1 unit towards Single Award Certifications.", and both the 160:1 and 240:1 sentences exactly as claimed. Album Award tiers are listed with the same four figures plus "*Note that different tiers are applicable to albums released before May 1, 2008." Album formula verbatim: "Digital & Physical Album Sales + TEA (Track Equivalent Album) + SEA (Stream Equivalent Album) = Total Units for Album Award Certification"; "TEA: 10 track downloads = 1 unit toward Certification."; "SEA: 1500 on-demand audio streams = 1 unit toward Certification." The requirements list contains, verbatim: "On-demand official video streams within Canada from an Approved DSP, occurring after January 1, 2020."

THIRD: https://musiccanada.com/gold-platinum/gold-platinum-video-faqs/ ("Official Video Integration"). Opening line: this document covers "the integration of official video views into Music Canada's Gold & Platinum criteria for Single Awards." Formula given as "Digital Song Sales (1:1) + Premium On-Demand Audio Streams (160:1) + Ad-Supported On-Demand Audio Streams (240:1) + Premium Official Video Streams (160:1) + Ad-Supported Official Video Streams (240:1)".

VERDICT: every figure in the claim reproduces exactly. Single 40k/80k/800k confirmed; album 40k/80k/800k confirmed for post-May-2008 releases; no Silver tier confirmed; the 9x ceiling then Diamond/Double Diamond/Triple Diamond confirmed; the whole Double-through-9x ladder matches cell for cell; every quoted sentence is verbatim; the singles-only video asymmetry is confirmed independently by the video FAQ's own scope statement and by the album SEA rule saying "on-demand audio streams". Arithmetic check: 19 x 80,000 = 1,520,000, and Music Canada names no such tier — correct.
verdict.corrections:
No figure is wrong. Six accuracy caveats worth carrying into publication:

1. MISSING LADDER, not a wrong one. The claim's album row states 40,000/80,000/800,000 with no date qualifier in the numeric fields (the "after 1 May 2008" caveat only appears later, in the multiplier prose). Music Canada publishes a SECOND, higher album ladder for albums released BEFORE May 1, 2008: Gold 50,000, Platinum 100,000, Double 200,000, Triple 300,000, Quadruple 400,000, Quintuple 500,000, 6x 600,000, 7x 700,000, 8x 800,000, 9x 900,000, Diamond 1,000,000, Double Diamond 2,000,000, Triple Diamond 3,000,000. Harmless for the Afrobeats board (every artist on it debuted well after 2008), but if the threshold table is ever rendered as a general reference the album row must carry the "released after May 1, 2008" qualifier or it is materially incomplete.

2. THE CITED URL DOESN'T CARRY ALL THE QUOTED TEXT. https://musiccanada.com/certification/ carries every NUMBER and the 160:1 / 240:1 / TEA / SEA footnotes, but it does NOT contain the two formula blocks, the "Digital and physical single sales count as 1 unit" sentence, the "Multi-Platinum: 160,000 Units (increments of 80,000 thereafter)" wording, or the January 1 2020 video line. Those are all on https://musiccanada.com/gold-platinum/faq/. Both are Music Canada's own site, so the body is right — but cite the FAQ alongside /certification/ rather than attributing the verbatim formula quotes to /certification/.

3. THE BODY CONTRADICTS ITSELF ON TEA. The FAQ says "TEA: 10 track downloads = 1 unit"; the Certification Definitions page says "Track Equivalent Album (TEA): 10 tracks sales = 1 unit". Downloads vs sales is not the same set (physical single sales). The claim quoted the FAQ, which is defensible, but don't present either wording as the single authoritative phrasing.

4. THE 160/240 SPLIT HAS A START DATE THE CLAIM OMITS. The video FAQ states: "Effective March 5, 2024, Music Canada will apply economic weighting to on-demand audio streams and official video streams..." So the premium/ad-supported split is only ~2.5 years old. Any Canadian certification awarded before 5 March 2024 was computed under the earlier flat ratio, not under 160:1/240:1. Do not retro-apply the current ratio to back-calculate older Canadian plaques.

5. VIDEO ELIGIBILITY WORDING DIFFERS BY PAGE. Main FAQ: "occurring after January 1, 2020". Video FAQ: "which occurred on or after January 1, 2020". Trivial, but the claim's verbatim quote is the main FAQ's.

6. SHARPEN THE >9x GUIDANCE. Diamond is exactly 10x Platinum (800,000), Double Diamond 20x (1,600,000), Triple Diamond 30x (2,400,000). So a hypothetical 19x-equivalent at 1,520,000 units sits ABOVE Diamond but BELOW Double Diamond — under Music Canada's own naming it is still "Diamond", not "Double Diamond". "Diamond-family naming" is right as far as it goes; the safer rule is: 800,000-1,599,999 = Diamond, 1,600,000-2,399,999 = Double Diamond, 2,400,000+ = Triple Diamond. Never render a Canadian award as "10x Platinum" through "19x Platinum" — Music Canada names no such tier.

Also confirmed as a non-issue: the single/album split is NOT conflated anywhere in the claim, and the singles-only video rule is correct and independently corroborated.

countries.body: SNEP — Syndicat National de l'Édition Phonographique
countries.sourceQuote: Les seuils — Singles (ÉQUIVALENCES Streams /streaming + téléchargements + ventes physiques): «Singles or : 15 millions D'ÉQUIVALENT streams / Singles platine : 30 millions D'ÉQUIVALENT streams / Singles diamant : 50 millions d'équivalent streams». Albums (ÉQUIVALENCES ventes (ventes physiques + streaming + téléchargements)): «Albums or : 50 000 équivalent ventes / Albums platine : 100 000 équivalent ventes / Albums double platine : 200 000 équivalent ventes / Albums triple platine : 300 000 équivalent ventes / Albums diamant : 500 000 équivalent ventes / Albums double diamant : 1 000 000 équivalent ventes / Albums triple diamant : 1 500 000 équivalent ventes / Albums quadruple diamant : 2 000 000 équivalent ventes».
countries.unitDefinition: Sales + streaming equivalents, with two DIFFERENT units for the two categories. SINGLES are counted in 'équivalent streams', not sales: SNEP's own wording is «Les téléchargements d'un titre sont convertis en équivalent streams (sur la base de 1 téléchargement = 150 streams) et sont ensuite ajoutés aux volumes de streaming de ce titre» — i.e. 1 download = 150 streams, added to the track's stream volume; the single thresholds (15M/30M/50M) are therefore stream counts, not unit counts. ALBUMS are counted in 'équivalent ventes': «les volumes d'écoutes en streaming de tous les titres d'un album sont cumulés. Ce total est converti en équivalent ventes (sur la base de 1500 streams = 1 vente) après avoir soustrait de ce total la moitié des streams du titre le plus écouté» — 1,500 streams = 1 album sale, after subtracting half the streams of the album's most-streamed track, then added to physical (CD & vinyl) and download sales. Which streams count has changed twice: from 27 April 2018 only premium (paid-subscription) listening counted; since July 2024 ad-funded (freemium) listening counts again at a discount — «Le ratio de conversion retenu pour cette intégration est de 7 streams freemium pour 1 stream premium» (7 freemium streams = 1 premium stream).
countries.multiplierRule: Not a uniform 'N x Platinum'. For ALBUMS the platinum ladder is literally N x 100,000 but stops at triple: platine 100,000, double platine 200,000, triple platine 300,000. There is no quadruple platine — the ladder jumps to diamant at 500,000 and then multiplies the DIAMOND threshold: double diamant 1,000,000 (2 x 500,000), triple diamant 1,500,000, quadruple diamant 2,000,000. Quadruple Diamant (2,000,000 équivalent ventes) is the ceiling: the SNEP certification database's own filter vocabulary is exactly Or, Double Or, Platine, Double Platine, Triple Platine, Diamant, Double Diamant, Triple Diamant, Quadruple Diamant — nothing above 4x diamond exists, and a query of the register returns exactly one Quadruple Diamant album (Stromae, 'Racine Carrée'). So France cannot carry anything like a 19x award; the highest French plaque possible is 4x Diamond = 2,000,000 units. For SINGLES no multiples are published at all: the seuils page defines only Or / Platine / Diamant. Filtering the register by category confirms singles carry Or, Platine and Diamant, with zero Triple Platine, zero Double Diamant and above; the only anomaly is two singles carrying 'Double Platine' (Jenifer 'Nouvelle Page', constat 12/12/2024; Sofiane 'Bandit Saleté', constat 23/05/2024), a tier SNEP does not define for singles on its thresholds page. 'Double Or' appears in the filter but SNEP's own history sheet records the album 'double or' as «Supprimé» in July 2009, so it is legacy only.
countries.diamondRule: Distinct published threshold at its own level, not a computed multiple of Platinum. For SINGLES, Diamant = 50,000,000 equivalent streams against a Platine of 30,000,000 — 1.67x Platinum, so it cannot be derived from the platinum figure. For ALBUMS, Diamant = 500,000 équivalent ventes; that happens to equal 5 x the 100,000 platine threshold, but SNEP lists it as its own named tier and the ladder skips the intervening 400,000 (there is no quadruple platine). France does award Diamond, heavily, and multiples of it up to Quadruple Diamant. SNEP's own history sheet dates the creation of the diamond single to January 1997, the album diamond to November 1988, the video diamond to August 1991, and double diamant «(et ses multiples)» to January 2014.
countries.changedSince2015: Yes — twice for singles-relevant rules and once for album thresholds, all inside the 2018–2026 window your plaques span. (1) JANUARY 2016: certifications became automatic and streaming was folded in («Depuis janvier 2016, les certifications décernées par le SNEP sont automatiquement générées en fonction des seuils de ventes atteints chaque semaine» / «C'est également depuis 2016 que performances des écoutes en streaming ont été intégrées aux certifications»). Album thresholds were cut at the same time, per SNEP's own history sheet: Or 75,000 -> 50,000; Platine 200,000 -> 100,000; Double platine 400,000 -> 200,000; Triple platine 600,000 -> 300,000; Diamant 750,000 -> 500,000 (the prior values had stood since July 2009); Double diamant stayed at 1,000,000. Album thresholds have NOT moved since. (2) 27 APRIL 2018: SNEP's own communiqué 'Tops et certifications : la valeur comme nouveau dénominateur commun' (published 25 April 2018, effective «À compter de ce vendredi 27 avril») restricted counting to premium streams and raised singles thresholds by 50%: «– OR : 15 millions d'équivalents streams (au lieu de 10M) – PLATINE : 30 millions d'équivalents streams (au lieu de 20M) – DIAMANT : 50 millions d'équivalents streams (au lieu de 35M)», adding «Les règles d'éligibilité aux certifications Albums ne sont pas modifiées». So any French single plaque dated before 27 Apr 2018 was earned at 10M/20M/35M, and from 27 Apr 2018 onward at 15M/30M/50M. (3) JANUARY 2018: video/DVD thresholds were cut (history sheet): Or 7,500 -> 5,000; Platine 15,000 -> 10,000; Double platine 30,000 -> 20,000; Triple platine 45,000 -> 30,000; Diamant 60,000 -> 40,000. (4) JULY 2024: freemium streams re-admitted at 7 freemium = 1 premium — a change to WHAT counts, not to the threshold numbers, which are unchanged since 27 Apr 2018 for singles and since Jan 2016 for albums.
countries.notes: Confirmed entirely on SNEP's own domain — the live thresholds page, SNEP's own April 2018 press release at https://snepmusique.com/actualites-du-snep/tops-et-certifications-la-valeur-comme-nouveau-denominateur-commun/, SNEP's own history sheet PDF at https://snepmusique.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/10/SNEP-tableau.pdf (linked from the thresholds page as «Historique des règles et seuils des certifications»), and the live certification register at https://snepmusique.com/les-certifications/ (which accepts ?certification=<tier>&categorie=<Singles|Albums|Vidéos> and exports CSV). NO Wikipedia or press was used for any value. ONE INTERNAL CONFLICT WORTH KNOWING: the 2019 history-sheet PDF prints the April 2018 singles Platine cell as '25 millions eq-stream', while SNEP's own April 2018 communiqué and the current live thresholds page both say 30 millions. Two SNEP sources beat one, and the live page is the current authority, so 30,000,000 is the figure I report; treat the history sheet's 25M cell as a typo in that PDF. THIRD CATEGORY: SNEP certifies 'Vidéos' as well as Singles and Albums — thresholds (from Jan 2018, history sheet) Vidéo or 5,000; Vidéo platine 10,000; Double vidéo platine 20,000; Triple vidéo platine 30,000; Vidéo diamant 40,000, in copies. These are the only category NOT automated: «Attention : les certifications des vidéos ne sont pas automatisées et peuvent être constatées par OCC sur demande au SNEP». There is no EP category and no separate 'streaming single' category. TOTAL CEILING CHECK for your 19x holdings: nothing in the French system exceeds Quadruple Diamant, so any French plaque above 4x diamond on the site is wrong by construction.

Singles platine : 30 millions D'ÉQUIVALENT streams
Singles diamant : 50 millions d'équivalent streams

Albums platine : 100 000 équivalent ventes
Albums double platine : 200 000 équivalent ventes
Albums triple platine : 300 000 équivalent ventes
Albums diamant : 500 000 équivalent ventes
Albums double diamant : 1 000 000 équivalent ventes
Albums triple diamant : 1 500 000 équivalent ventes
Albums quadruple diamant : 2 000 000 équivalent ventes"

Same page, methodology, verbatim: "Les téléchargements d'un titre sont convertis en équivalent streams (sur la base de 1 téléchargement = 150 streams) et sont ensuite ajoutés aux volumes de streaming de ce titre." — "Méthode de conversion streaming/ventes d'albums depuis janvier 2016 : les volumes d'écoutes en streaming de tous les titres d'un album sont cumulés. Ce total est converti en équivalent ventes (sur la base de 1500 streams = 1 vente) après avoir soustrait de ce total la moitié des streams du titre le plus écouté." — "Depuis juillet 2024 : les écoutes en streaming premium (abonnements payants) ainsi que les écoutes en streaming issues de la consommation freemium (financées par la publicité) sont prises en compte […] Le ratio de conversion retenu pour cette intégration est de 7 streams freemium pour 1 stream premium."

No "argent"/silver tier appears anywhere on the page or in the register filters — grep for argent|silver returns zero hits on both. Silver = null is correct.

SECONDARY (all SNEP's own site):
1. https://snepmusique.com/les-certifications/ — register filter markup read from raw HTML. data-id values are exactly: Or, Double Or, Platine, Double Platine, Triple Platine, Diamant, Double Diamant, Triple Diamant, Quadruple Diamant. Categories: Singles, Albums, Vidéos. Nothing above Quadruple Diamant exists, so a 19x French plaque is impossible.
2. Register query ?certification=Quadruple%20Diamant&categorie=Albums → exactly one row: RACINE CARREE / STROMAE / MERCURY / UNIVERSAL MUSIC FRANCE, sortie 30/09/2013, constat 23/12/2015.
3. Register query ?certification=Triple%20Platine,Double%20Diamant,Triple%20Diamant,Quadruple%20Diamant&categorie=Singles → "Désolé, aucun résultat ne correspond à vos critères de sélection". Zero singles at or above Triple Platine.
4. Register query ?certification=Double%20Platine&categorie=Singles → exactly two rows: NOUVELLE PAGE / JENIFER (constat 12/12/2024) and BANDIT SALETÉ / SOFIANE (constat 23/05/2024). The claimed anomaly is real and complete.
5. https://snepmusique.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/10/SNEP-tableau.pdf ("Historique des règles et seuils", linked from the seuils page). No pdftotext on this machine, so I decompressed the content streams and reconstructed the tables from the Tm coordinates. Albums sheet shows the DOUBLE ALBUM OR column ending in "Supprimé"; register confirms Double Or albums are legacy only (Depeche Mode "Playing the Angel", Il Divo, Ilona Mitrecey — all constats 13/12/2005).
6. https://snepmusique.com/actualites-du-snep/tops-et-certifications-la-valeur-comme-nouveau-denominateur-commun/ (SNEP communiqué, 25 April 2018) — confirms both the date and the singles numbers verbatim: "À compter de ce vendredi 27 avril […] pour ne prendre en compte que les seules écoutes en streaming issues de la consommation premium" and "Les nouveaux seuils des certifications Singles sont les suivants : – OR : 15 millions d'équivalents streams (au lieu de 10M) – PLATINE : 30 millions d'équivalents streams (au lieu de 20M) – DIAMANT : 50 millions d'équivalents streams (au lieu de 35M)", introduced as "un réajustement à la hausse de +50% des seuils des seules certifications singles" with "Les règles d'éligibilité aux certifications Albums ne sont pas modifiées."

Every figure and every structural assertion in the claim reproduces off SNEP's own pages. The single/album unit split is not conflated: SNEP itself labels the single ladder "ÉQUIVALENCES Streams" and the album ladder "ÉQUIVALENCES ventes".
verdict.corrections:
No corrections to any figure — all four singles values, all four album values, both conversion ratios, the freemium ratio, the ladder shape, the 4x Diamant ceiling and both register anomalies reproduce exactly.

One trap found that is worth recording so nobody "corrects" this figure downward later. SNEP contradicts itself on the single Platine threshold. Its own historique PDF (https://snepmusique.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/10/SNEP-tableau.pdf, linked from the very bottom of the thresholds page as "Historique des règles et seuils des certifications") shows the Avril 2018 singles row as 15 / 25 / 50 millions eq-stream. I verified this by column position, not by text order — the OR/PLATINE/DIAMANT columns sit at x≈276, x≈380, x≈485, and the Avril 2018 row's "25 millions" sits at x=380.1, squarely in the PLATINE column. So the PDF really does say 25M, not 30M.

The PDF is wrong, not the claim. Three things settle it: (a) the live seuils page says 30 millions; (b) SNEP's own 2018 communiqué says "PLATINE : 30 millions d'équivalents streams (au lieu de 20M)"; (c) that communiqué frames the change as "+50%", and 20M x 1.5 = 30M, which the PDF's own 25M figure contradicts internally while 30M satisfies it, exactly as 10→15 and 35→50 do. The 2019 PDF graphic simply carries a typo.

Two minor notes, neither a disagreement:
- The claim's "27 April 2018" date is not on the thresholds page itself (which says only "Avril 2018" / "Depuis juillet 2024"). It is however confirmed verbatim by SNEP's own communiqué of 25 April 2018 — "À compter de ce vendredi 27 avril" — so the date stands on the body's own site.
- Silver = null is right for the current ladder, but note SNEP historically did have a single tier called "argent": the historique PDF records "Création du single d'argent" in Juillet 1985. It was discontinued and appears in neither the current seuils nor the register's filter vocabulary, so it must not be revived as an FR Silver threshold.

countries.body: Recorded Music NZ (RMNZ), which compiles and publishes the Official Aotearoa Music Charts
countries.sourceQuote: Chart Rules (as at 30 September 2025), rule 2.4 Certification: "Gold and Platinum status will be awarded to Albums, Singles and Compilations based on all chart-eligible consumer consumption, as verified by the Chart Compiler... The following certification thresholds, expressed in sales equivalent terms, shall apply: Format / Gold Status / Platinum Status — Single 15,000 points (sales equivalent) 30,000 (sales equivalent); Album 7,500 points (sales equivalent) 15,000 (sales equivalent)." And the parallel table: "Single 1,500,000 points (paid stream equivalent) 3,000,000 (paid stream equivalent); Album 750,000 points (paid stream equivalent) 1,500,000 (paid stream equivalent)." The same figures appear on RMNZ's own About page: "Gold — Singles 15,000 chart points, Albums 7,500 chart points; Platinum — Singles 30,000 chart points, Albums 15,000 chart points."
countries.unitDefinition: Sales plus streaming equivalents, expressed as 'points' / 'chart points' (sales-equivalent units), not pure sales. RMNZ: "Gold and Platinum certifications are awarded once a release hits our qualifying thresholds, which are based on chart-eligible retail sales (physical and digital) and paid stream equivalent data." Rule 2.4 adds that certification uses the same machinery as the chart: "The same base streaming Conversion Rate and calculations used for chart positions shall apply for certification determination. However, the neutralising step (reducing the top two singles to the average of the next eight) described at Rule 5.1(b)ii shall not be applied." CRUCIALLY, RMNZ DOES NOT PUBLISH THE STREAM-TO-SALE RATIO AS A NUMBER. Rule 5.3: "This conversion rate is calculated using both premium and ad-supported streaming data which produces a combined sales equivalent for the Charts. Depending on the number of ad-supported to premium streams the combined ratio will vary. This ratio is set at the discretion of the Chart Committee... These ratios will be reviewed on a biannual basis." So the live ratio is a moving, unpublished committee number — any fixed figure such as '175 streams = 1 sale' circulating in secondary sources is NOT confirmable at the body and I have not adopted it. The only ratio RMNZ itself publishes is implied by its own second table: 1,500,000 paid streams = 15,000 single points and 750,000 paid streams = 7,500 album points, i.e. 100 paid streams = 1 point in both cases. Albums additionally go through the Stream Equivalent Album formula (rule 5.1(b)): the singles conversion rate is applied, a neutralising factor reduces the two most-streamed tracks to the average of the next eight (this step is disapplied for certification), and the top 10 tracks' combined value is divided by 10; albums not streamable in their entirety have SEA points reset to zero. Streams under 30 seconds and non-interactive/algorithmic listening are excluded (5.3.1).
countries.multiplierRule: NOT PUBLISHED. RMNZ's rules and its About page define exactly two statuses — Gold and Platinum — and give one threshold for each. Neither the Chart Rules (30 Sep 2025 or the Nov 2024 and Nov 2023 editions I also read) nor the About page nor the FAQ contains the words 'multi-platinum', '2x Platinum', 'Diamond' or any formula for awards above Platinum. I searched all three rules editions for those strings and got zero hits. RMNZ does publicise multi-platinum figures in practice, but it does not publish a rule saying what 2x or 3x means, so I am reporting no rule rather than assuming the obvious N x 30,000 / N x 15,000. If you need the multiplier to price NZ plaques, treat 'N x Platinum = N x 30,000 points (singles) / N x 15,000 points (albums)' as an UNSOURCED working assumption and flag it as such — it is the natural reading of a body that publishes a single Platinum threshold, but the body itself never states it.
countries.diamondRule: There is no Diamond tier at RMNZ. Rule 2.4 awards only "Gold and Platinum status", the About page lists only Gold and Platinum, and the FAQ entry is titled "How do Gold and Platinum certifications work?". The word 'Diamond' does not appear anywhere in the Chart Rules (checked in the 30 Sep 2025, Nov 2024 and Nov 2023 editions). New Zealand therefore never awards Diamond — any Diamond plaque attributed to NZ on the site is wrong.
countries.changedSince2015: NOT CONFIRMABLE BEFORE 2023 AT THE BODY; NO CHANGE SINCE. I read three successive editions of RMNZ's own Chart Rules and the thresholds are byte-identical across all of them: 'Chart Rules (as at November 2023)', 'CHART RULES (as at 30 October 2024)' and 'CHART RULES (as at 30 September 2025)' all print Single 15,000 / 30,000 and Album 7,500 / 15,000 sales-equivalent, and Single 1,500,000 / 3,000,000 and Album 750,000 / 1,500,000 paid-stream-equivalent. RMNZ's own news post announcing the latest refresh, 'Refreshed Chart Rules – What's Changed' (1 October 2025, https://recordedmusic.co.nz/news/refreshed-chart-rules-whats-changed), enumerates every change made and certification thresholds are not among them — the changes were pre-sales at official events, delayed deliveries, catalogue re-entry extended from 10 to 13 weeks, an Aotearoa-eligibility definition, and compilation clarifications. So the thresholds are stable at least Nov 2023 to today (10 Sep 2026). For 2015–2023 I could NOT confirm anything at the body: RMNZ hosts no rules edition older than the March 2023 one on its current sites (the recordedmusic.co.nz copy of that March 2023 PDF now 404s to an HTML error page), and the Internet Archive was returning '429 Too Many Requests' and then a 'Temporarily Offline' page while I was checking, so archived captures of RMNZ's own older pages were unavailable. Secondary sources claim a June 2016 change that set exactly these figures; I have deliberately NOT adopted that, since it is not confirmable at RMNZ. Practical read for your 2018–2026 plaques: the two editions either side of the window that I could read agree, and there is no RMNZ statement of any change, so 15,000/30,000 and 7,500/15,000 is the safest single basis — but the pre-2023 gap is a genuine unverified stretch, not a confirmed 'no change'.
countries.notes: Both RMNZ sources used are first-party: aotearoamusiccharts.co.nz is RMNZ's own charts site (every page footer reads 'The Official Aotearoa Music Chart © Recorded Music NZ') and recordedmusic.co.nz is the body itself. No Wikipedia, wiki or blog value was used. CATEGORY DETAIL: the November 2023 and October 2024 rules also listed a third format row, 'Compilation 7,500 points (sales equivalent) 15,000 (sales equivalent)' / '750,000 / 1,500,000 (paid stream equivalent)', at the same numbers as Albums. The 30 September 2025 edition DROPS the Compilation row from both tables (the Compilations Chart was retired; rule 4.3 is now titled 'Excluded Compilations'), though rule 2.4's opening sentence still says status is awarded to 'Albums, Singles and Compilations'. There is no EP, video/DVD or separate 'streaming single' certification category in the current rules — RMNZ's DVD/music-video Gold and Platinum figures that circulate on secondary sites (2,500 / 5,000) appear NOWHERE in RMNZ's own published rules or About page, so I have not reported them. Certification cadence: 'Certification updates will be carried out on a weekly basis and apply immediately' and 'All releases are automatically eligible for certification' — NZ is an automatic register, unlike the request-based ones. A useful cross-check for your plaque pricing: because certification disapplies the neutralising step but the chart applies it, an album's certification points and its chart points are not the same number.

verdict.corrections:
No corrections — every figure in the claim reproduces exactly from RMNZ's own documents, the source URL is the body's own site, and the single/album split is not conflated (singles 15,000/30,000; albums 7,500/15,000, correctly the lower pair for albums). That row is absent from the table in the 30 Sep 2025 edition even though the sentence above it still names Compilations, so a compilation should be priced at album thresholds. Worth recording if the dataset ever distinguishes compilations from albums.

2. THE 100:1 IS EVEN WEAKER THAN THE CLAIM ALLOWS, WHICH STRENGTHENS THE CLAIM'S CAUTION. The 2025 PDF puts an asterisk under the two tables: "The streaming to sales conversion rate for Singles is set by the Chart Committee under Rule 5.3". So RMNZ itself flags the paid-stream table as downstream of a committee-set rate rather than as a fixed published equivalence. The 100:1 is a current illustrative figure implied by the table, not a locked rule — exactly as the claim treats it. The claim's refusal to adopt the secondary-source "175 streams = 1 sale" is correct: that string does not appear in any of the three editions.

3. WORDING DRIFT BETWEEN EDITIONS, worth knowing if this is re-verified later. The 2025 edition says the first table is "expressed in sales equivalent terms"; the 2023 and 2024 editions said "expressed in either sales or paid stream equivalent terms". The 2025 edition also added the cross-reference "described at Rule 5.1(b)ii" to the neutralising-step carve-out, which the older editions lacked. The claim quotes the 2025 wording accurately.

4. MINOR ATTRIBUTION DETAIL. The sentence the claim attributes to RMNZ — "chart-eligible retail sales (physical and digital) and paid stream equivalent data" — is verbatim from the About page. The PDF's own FAQ phrases it as "chart-eligible sales (physical and digital)", without "retail". Same meaning; the quotation is correctly sourced to the About page.

On the multiplier: I confirm the claim's finding as a negative result, not an omission. There is no published rule above Platinum anywhere on the body's site or in any of the three rules editions. Flagging "N x Platinum = N x 30,000 / N x 15,000 points" as an UNSOURCED working assumption is the right call and should be carried through to anything that prices NZ plaques above 1x Platinum.

countries.body: RIAA (Recording Industry Association of America)
countries.unitDefinition: Sales PLUS streaming equivalents, at different ratios for albums and singles. RIAA's own wording: for the Full-Length Album Award and Shortform Album/EP Award, "Album sales, single sales and on-demand audio and/or video streams are calculated at the formula of 1,500 on-demand audio and/or video streams = 10 track sales = 1 album sale." For the Digital Single Award, "Both downloads and on-demand audio and/or video single streams are counted towards the required thresholds. The formula of 150 on-demand streams is equivalent to one download sale." RIAA's official album-award audit PDF restates it per-unit: "Each permanent digital album or physical album sale count as 1 Unit"; "10 permanent track downloads from the album count as 1 Unit"; "1,500 on-demand audio and/or video streams from the album count as 1 Unit". Single-award PDF: "Each permanent digital download counts as 1 Unit"; "150 on-demand audio and/or video streams will count as 1 Unit". Only US sales/streams qualify; only official label/artist videos count, not UGC; non-interactive streams excluded.
countries.multiplierRule: Literally N times the Platinum threshold: 1,000,000 units per Platinum step. RIAA's Certification Levels table gives Multi-Platinum as "2,000,000 (in increments of 1,000,000 thereafter)", and the per-category tables say the award is "Recertified at each subsequent million units." So a 19x Platinum plaque = 19,000,000 units. The Digital Single Award PDF adds that even above Diamond the count continues "(increments of 1,000,000 thereafter)".
countries.diamondRule: Diamond is a named, distinct tier but its value is numerically 10x Platinum: "Diamond® 10,000,000 units", date established 1999. It sits on the same one-million-unit ladder (recertified at each million thereafter), so a title can be described either as Diamond or as 10x Platinum. NOTE an internal inconsistency on RIAA's own page: the master Certification Levels table and the Digital Single Award table both say Diamond = 10,000,000 units, but the Full-Length Album, Shortform Album/EP and Multi-Disc Set tables on the same page print "Diamond 2,000,000 units". RIAA's own current Album Award audit-requirements PDF resolves it in favour of 10,000,000 ("Diamond – 10,000,000 Units"), which is why 10,000,000 is reported here for albums.
countries.changedSince2015: The unit THRESHOLDS have not moved in the last decade. RIAA's own Certification Levels table dates them: Gold 500,000 (1958), Platinum 1,000,000 (1976), Multi-Platinum 2,000,000 (1984), Diamond 10,000,000 (1999). What changed is what counts as a unit. RIAA's own press release (RIAA DEBUTS ALBUM AWARD WITH STREAMS, © 2016 RIAA) states: "Effective Feb. 1, RIAA will include on-demand audio and video streams and a track sale equivalent in Gold & Platinum (G&P's) Album Award", setting "the new Album Award formula of 1,500 on-demand audio and/or video song streams = 10 track sales = 1 album sale", and on the same date "RIAA's Digital Single Award ratio will be updated from 100 on-demand streams = 1 download to 150 on-demand streams = 1 download". It also notes streams were first added to the Digital Single Award in 2013 (at 100:1). So: plaques earned before 1 Feb 2016 used pure sales for albums and a 100:1 stream ratio for singles; everything from 1 Feb 2016 to today (including every 2018-2026 plaque on this site) uses 1,500:1 for albums and 150:1 for singles, against unchanged 500k/1M/2M/10M thresholds. Caveat on the press-release citation: that URL now redirects to RIAA's site search after a site redesign, so the wording above was read from an archived copy of RIAA's own page; the live riaa.com pages and PDFs independently confirm the 1,500:1 and 150:1 ratios and all four thresholds.
countries.notes: Categories beyond album/single, all from the same RIAA page and all sales+stream-eligible unless stated: Shortform Album/EP (Gold 500,000, Platinum 1,000,000; 3-5 different songs, max 30 min run time); Multi-Disc Set (Gold 500,000, Platinum 1,000,000; two or more discs, min 100 min; each disc in the set counts as one unit); Music Video Single (Gold 25,000, Platinum 50,000, then each subsequent 50,000 — "1 unit = 1 physical sale and excludes streaming and digital sales"); Music Video Longform (Gold 50,000, Platinum 100,000, physical only); Multi-Box Music Video Set (Gold 50,000, Platinum 100,000); Master Ringtone Award (Gold at 500,000 ringtones). SEPARATE LATIN PROGRAM ("Premios de Oro y Platino", for releases with more than 50% Spanish-language lyrics, established 2001): Oro 30,000 units, Platino 60,000 (increments of 60,000 thereafter), Diamante 600,000 — same 1,500:1 stream formula. Do not apply Latin figures to a general-market Burna Boy title. Other rules that affect whether a plaque is even eligible: physical albums qualify 30 days after release, digital at release; pre-orders don't count until delivered; merch/ticket bundles need a $6-per-album retail premium and the standalone product must be separately purchasable; remixes/live/alternate versions are ineligible for single certification unless on an album version; a track's streams cannot be double-counted toward two different albums. Two further official RIAA PDFs corroborate the figures: https://www.riaa.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/09/ALBUM-AWARD-RIAA-AND-GRF-CERTIFICATION-AUDIT-REQUIREMENTS52.pdf and https://www.riaa.com/wp-content/uploads/2016/02/DIGITAL-SINGLE-AWARD-RIAA-AND-GRF-CERTIFICATION-AUDIT-REQUIREMENTS.pdf

The formula of 150 on-demand streams is equivalent to one download sale." — Gold "500,000 units", Platinum/Multi "1,000,000 units / Recertified at each million units", Diamond "10,000,000 units / Recertified at each million unit sales level". The numbers in the claim are, I believe, operationally CORRECT -- but the claim is mis-sourced on one of them, and the cited page will actively contradict anyone who checks it. That is why agrees=false, not because 10,000,000 is wrong.

1) THE REAL PROBLEM -- album Diamond. The claim says album Diamond = 10,000,000 and cites https://www.riaa.com/gold-platinum/about-awards/. That page's Full-Length Album Award, Shortform Album/EP Award and Multi-Disc Set tables all print "Diamond | 2,000,000 units". The page contradicts itself: its own top-level Certification Levels table says Diamond = 10,000,000 units, and every RIAA/GR&F audit PDF (2016, 2022, 2023) says "Diamond - 10,000,000 Units" for the Album Award. 10,000,000 is the operative figure -- RIAA awards album Diamond at 10 million, and 2,000,000 is a stale/erroneous cell on the marketing page (it looks like the old "Multi-Platinum 2,000,000" row mislabelled "Diamond" in all three album tables). ACTION: keep 10,000,000, but re-cite album Diamond to https://www.riaa.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/09/ALBUM-AWARD-RIAA-AND-GRF-CERTIFICATION-AUDIT-REQUIREMENTS52.pdf (and/or the Certification Levels table on the same page), and leave a note in the data so a future checker does not "correct" album Diamond down to 2,000,000 off the about-awards table. Do not publish 2,000,000.

2) Mis-attributed quote in the multiplier rule. The claim says "The Digital Single Award PDF adds that even above Diamond the count continues '(increments of 1,000,000 thereafter)'." In the CURRENT (2023/09) single PDF that parenthetical sits on the Platinum line only -- "Platinum - 1,000,000 Units (increments of 1,000,000 thereafter)" -- and the Diamond line carries no parenthetical at all. Only the older 2016 PDF puts "(increments of 1,000,000 thereafter)" on the Diamond line. Above-Diamond continuation is still supported, but by a different sentence: the about-awards Digital Single table's Diamond row says "Recertified at each million unit sales level". Fix the attribution or the multiplier rule quotes a line that is not where the claim says it is.

3) Small wording drifts, worth tightening but not disqualifying on their own:
   - "official label/artist videos" -> RIAA says "official label/company videos".
   - "non-interactive streams excluded" is an inference, not page wording; RIAA only ever specifies on-demand streams.
   - "Recertified at each subsequent million units" is the album/shortform/multi-disc wording; the Digital Single table says "Recertified at each million units" (no "subsequent").
   - Full-Length wording is "Album sales, single sales and on-demand..."; Shortform has the serial comma ("Album sales, single sales, and on-demand..."). If those strings are stored as quotes, store them per-award.

4) Confirmed correct, no change needed: Silver = null for both single and album (RIAA has no Silver tier); single Gold 500,000 / Platinum 1,000,000 / Diamond 10,000,000; album Gold 500,000 / Platinum 1,000,000; the 1,500:10:1 album formula and the 150:1 single formula, correctly kept distinct (no single/album conflation); Multi-Platinum = N x 1,000,000; US-only sales/streams; official videos only.

5) Not an error, but a gap: the same page defines a separate Latin program (Oro 30,000 / Platino 60,000 / Multi-Platino 120,000 in increments of 60,000 / Diamante 600,000) for releases with >50% Spanish-language lyrics. If the dataset carries one US row with the general thresholds, it should say so explicitly, or a Latin-certified title will be scored against the wrong ladder.

countries.body: RiSA (Recording Industry of South Africa)
countries.unitDefinition: Sales PLUS streaming, and RiSA publishes BOTH a stream-to-unit conversion and a parallel pure-stream threshold column. Conversions, verbatim from the Digital Sales section: Downloads — "1 Permanent Download = 1 Single", "10 Permanent Downloads = 1 Album"; Subscription Streaming — "125 Streams = 1 Single", "1,250 Streams = 1 Album"; AD Supported Streaming — "875 Streams = 1 Single", "8,750 Streams = 1 Album" (i.e. ad-funded streams are worth 1/7th of a subscription stream). Mobile Sales — "22 Master Tones or Ringback Tones = 1 Single; and 220 Master Tones or Ringback Tones = 1 Album". Separately, each threshold row carries an equivalent all-stream figure: for sales after 1 Jan 2024, album Gold is "25,000 units" or "30 million streams", album Platinum "50,000 units" or "60 million streams"; single/EP Gold "20,000 units" or "2.4 million streams", Platinum "40,000 units" or "4.8 million streams". Excluded from the stream count: foreign streams ("only consider sales in SA"), non-interactive/webcast streams, UGC, tethered/temporary downloads, cloud-locker activity, iTunes Radio, full give-aways, and "all Short-form/ social media content, including: TikTok, Facebook Reels etc." Certification is on firm invoiced sales; promo/free copies do not qualify.
countries.multiplierRule: Literally N times Platinum, expressed as a fixed increment per step. Albums (post-2024): Platinum 50,000 and "For Double or Multi-Platinum Awards, Increase by: 50,000 units" — so Nx Platinum = N x 50,000 units (or N x 60 million streams). Singles/EPs (post-2024): Platinum 40,000, "Double Platinum 80,000 units", "Multi-Platinum Award, Increase by: 40,000 units" — so Nx Platinum = N x 40,000 units. Pre-2024 awards use the old increments: 30,000 per step for albums, 20,000 per step for singles. The application form asks for "Level Requested: Gold / Platinum / Double Platinum / Multi-Platinum" — those are the only levels named anywhere in the document.
countries.diamondRule: No Diamond tier at all. The word "Diamond" does not appear anywhere in RiSA's Certification Levels document; the ladder is Gold, Platinum, Double Platinum, Multi-Platinum only. Any "Diamond" claim for a South African plaque is not a RiSA award level.
countries.changedSince2015: YES — and this is the single most important fact for pricing 2018-2026 plaques. RiSA roughly DOUBLED its thresholds for sales after 1 January 2024, and its own tables print both regimes side by side under the headings "Sales Prior to 31st December 2023" and "Sales After 1st January 2024". ALBUMS: Gold went 15,000 -> 25,000 units (18 million -> 30 million streams); Platinum 30,000 -> 50,000 units (36 million -> 60 million streams); the Double/Multi-Platinum increment 30,000 -> 50,000 units. SINGLES & EPs: Gold 10,000 -> 20,000 units (1.2 million -> 2.4 million streams); Platinum 20,000 -> 40,000 units (2.4 million -> 4.8 million streams); Double Platinum 40,000 -> 80,000 units (4.8 million -> 9.6 million streams); the Multi-Platinum increment 20,000 -> 40,000 units. So any RiSA plaque awarded on sales up to 31 Dec 2023 (i.e. most 2018-2023 awards on this site) was earned against the LOWER figures; only awards on post-1 Jan 2024 sales use 25,000/50,000 and 20,000/40,000. The stream-conversion ratios have also moved within the last decade: a RiSA-operated origin host still serving an older revision of the same document (https://risa-prod.trafficmanager.net/website/certification/levels/) gives Subscription "120 Streams = 1 Single / 1200 Streams = 1 Album" and AD Supported "720 Streams = 1 Single / 7200 Streams = 1 Album", versus 125/1,250 and 875/8,750 on the live page — RiSA does not date that ratio change, so do not attach a date to it.
countries.notes: READING THE SITE: risa.org.za actively defeats non-browser fetching. Plain HTTP requests to https://risa.org.za/certification-levels/ return HTTP 200 with an 861-byte decoy page titled "ai/certification-levels/" containing scrambled Shakespeare/Dostoevsky prose and fake links — an AI-crawler tarpit, not the real page. The real content is JS-rendered and was read by loading the URL in an actual browser. Anyone re-verifying with curl/WebFetch will get the decoy and may wrongly conclude the page has no numbers. CAUTION ON THE MIRROR: RiSA's origin host risa-prod.trafficmanager.net serves the real HTML to plain fetches, but the copy at /website/certification/levels/ is an OLDER revision (different stream ratios, different exclusion list). Treat risa.org.za as canonical. OTHER CATEGORIES, all from the same document: Multi-box audio sets (3+ units per box) Gold 12,500 / Platinum 25,000, increments of 25,000, and the whole box counts as 1 unit; Music Videos Gold 5,000 / Platinum 10,000, increments of 10,000; DVDs Gold 10,000 / Platinum 20,000, increments of 20,000. These three carry no dual pre/post-2024 table and no stream equivalent. EPs are certified on the SINGLES table, not the album table — a Burna Boy EP takes 20,000/40,000, not 25,000/50,000. Double albums and cassettes count as one unit. Compilations qualify but "awards may only be presented to the record companies and NOT the artist(s) or producer(s)". Certification is open to RiSA member companies only and is request-based (application by letter signed by the FD and MD, then a third-party audit), so absence from the register is not evidence a threshold was not met. The mention of "gold and silver foil" on the page refers to the physical hologram seal stock, NOT a Silver award tier.
