countries.unitDefinition: Sales + streaming equivalents, in 'Einheiten'. Guideline Ziff. 6: '1 Single-CD = 1 Einheit / 1 Single-Vinyl-Schallplatte = 1 Einheit / 1 Download = 1 Einheit / Anzahl Premium-Streams / Beimischungsfaktor = 1 Einheit / Anzahl Ad-funded Streams / Beimischungsfaktor = 1 Einheit (ab 01.01.23)'. The Beimischungsfaktor depends on the release date of the product; the guideline's own table gives, from 01.01.2023: subscription/premium 1:161 (161 premium streams = 1 unit) and ad-funded 1:1'185. For albums: 'Sämtliche Subscription Streams werden zusammengezählt und durch die Anzahl Titel auf dem Album und dem Beimischungsfaktor «Subscription-Streams» geteilt' (i.e. total album streams ÷ number of tracks ÷ 161). Physical album sales are grossed up: 'Bei den physischen Albumverkäufen wird eine Deckungsrate von 19% ... hinzugerechnet.' Only domestic (Inland) sales count; exports and special offers are excluded. Verification is performed by GfK on IFPI Schweiz's behalf (CHF 75 fee).
countries.multiplierRule: Literally N x the Platinum threshold, and the guideline enumerates each step explicitly: singles Doppelplatin 60'000 (2x30'000), 3-fach 90'000, 4-fach 120'000, 5-fach 150'000; albums 40'000 / 60'000 / 80'000 / 100'000. IMPORTANT: the table stops at 5-fach Platin — IFPI Schweiz publishes no tier above 5x, so any award above 5x on this site is NOT covered by a published Swiss threshold (the linear pattern is an inference, not a published value).
countries.diamondRule: No Diamond at all. The Edelmetall-Richtlinie's category list (Ziff. 5) contains only Gold, Platin and multiples of Platin; 'Diamant' does not appear anywhere in the guideline or on the Edelmetallprüfung page.
countries.changedSince2015: Not stated. The current guideline is dated 'Stand: Juli 2024' and does NOT document any change to the unit thresholds, nor give any previous values. What IFPI Schweiz does date is the stream mixing factor (Beimischungsfaktor), whose full history it publishes: ab 01.04.2014 = 178; ab 01.04.2015 = 116; ab 01.01.2016 = 114; ab 01.10.2016 = 108; ab 01.08.2017 = 119; ab 01.01.2018 = 127; ab 01.01.2019 = 148; ab 01.03.2020 = 175; ab 01.03.2021 = 176; ab 01.02.2022 = 174; ab 01.01.2023 = 161 — plus ad-funded streams becoming eligible ab 01.01.2023 at 1:1'185. The factor applied is 'der Beimischungsfaktor zum Zeitpunkt der Erstveröffentlichung' (the one in force at first release), so a 2018 plaque and a 2026 plaque use different stream maths even though the unit thresholds are the same. I checked the Internet Archive for an older IFPI Schweiz thresholds page (www.ifpi.ch/?section=goldplatin, 2018 capture): the archived page does not carry the numbers, so no body-published earlier value could be obtained.
countries.notes: Read at the body: guideline PDF linked from https://www.ifpi.ch/edelmetallpruefung ('Richtlinien Edelmetall, Mindestgrenzen und Berechnungsbeispiele finden Sie hier'). EXTRA CATEGORIES: (1) French- and Italian-language album repertoire has its own, lower thresholds — 'Alben-Repertoire in französischer und italienischer Sprache: Gold = 7'500 Einheiten, Platin = 15'000 Einheiten' — so a francophone/italophone album plaque is NOT the 10'000/20'000 figure. (2) Musikfilme (DVD/Blu-ray/video streaming): Gold 3'000, Platin 6'000. No EP category and no separate 'streaming single' category. Sales categories that aggregate: singles = CDs, vinyl, download, audio streaming; albums = CDs, MCs, vinyl, download, audio streaming. Note a wording mismatch worth knowing: the PDF says the guidelines are 'verbindlich' (binding) for all producers, while the website page calls them 'unverbindliche Orientierungshilfe'. Awards are physically handed out by the labels themselves; only the officialised emblem certifies GfK verification. Digital sales before 2022 and ad-funded streams must always be evidenced with documents.

countries.body: Audiogest (issuer of the galardões under the AFP/Audiogest TOP regime; AFP – Associação Fonográfica Portuguesa has no live website)
countries.sourceQuote: Anexo III, Tabela 1 — 'Tabelas de unidades para obtenção de Galardões'. SINGLE, vigência 'semana 27/2025': OURO 'SINGLE: 12 000 / Streams (*): 3 300 000'; PLATINA 'SINGLE: 25 000 / Streams (*): 6 800 000'; DIAMANTE 'SINGLE: 250 000 / Streams (*): 68 000 000'. ÁLBUM, coluna 'Unidades Álbuns (a partir de 01/01/2024)': OURO 3 500, PLATINA 7 000, DIAMANTE 70 000. Cover page: 'Aprovado na Assembleia Geral de 23 de Janeiro de 2024 e alterado na Assembleia Geral de 2 de Julho de 2025.'
countries.unitDefinition: Sales + streaming, expressed as 'UNIDADES DE CONSUMO'. Two conversions apply. (1) Ad-supported vs subscription streams are equalised by the Taxa de Conversão do Stream; the regulation's own 'Ponto 3 – Tabelas de conversão' gives, 'da semana 14 de 2025 até à data atual': Streaming Suportado por Assinatura = 1, Streaming Suportado por Publicidade = 1/4.7 = 0,21, Full Track Download (FTD) = 103, Single = 103 — i.e. 103 subscription-equalised streams = 1 single unit, and an ad-supported stream is worth 0.21 of a subscription stream. (Weeks 1/2024–13/2025 the same table read: ad-supported 1/6.1 = 0,16 and FTD/Single = 213.) (2) Albums: only the 12 highest-streamed tracks count; the mean of tracks 3–12 replaces the real stream counts of tracks 1 and 2; the total is divided by the stream-to-single ratio and then by 12 (or by the track count if under 12) to give 'unidades de Álbuns Digitais'. The Streams (*) figures printed in the award table are explicitly a 'Simulação efetuada com base na proporção dos tipos de consumo e no peso económico dos streams', not a second independent threshold. Physical album units only count if sold at >= EUR 5,95.
countries.multiplierRule: Awards are 'atribuídas, sucessiva e não cumulativamente'. Art. 16.3: 'Contam para novo Galardão, as vendas físicas, digitais ou por qualquer outro canal, que tenham ocorrido desde a atribuição do último Galardão' — each further Platinum requires another full Platinum quantum of consumption measured from the previous award, so Nx Platinum is N times the Platinum figure in aggregate. HARD CAP (added July 2025): 'A emissão de galardões de platina encontra-se limitada a um máximo de cinco atribuições por faixa ou álbum. Ultrapassado esse limite, qualquer novo pedido de certificação deverá corresponder obrigatoriamente ao galardão de diamante.' So Portugal now publishes no tier above 5x Platinum. Also: awards can only be granted up to 5 years after release (7 years for Diamante), and 'Os galardões atribuídos com base nas tabelas em vigor até à semana em que foram alterados os consumos mínimos mantêm-se' — old plaques stand at the threshold in force when granted.
countries.diamondRule: Diamante is a distinct published threshold, not merely Nx Platina: 250 000 single units / 70 000 album units. It did not exist for singles before week 01/2024 (the pre-2024 single table shows '-' in the DIAMANTE column). Since July 2025 it is also the compulsory next step once five Platinas have been issued for a title, and it has a longer eligibility window (7 years from release vs 5).
countries.changedSince2015: Yes, twice in the period the plaques span, both dated by the body. ALBUMS: 'Unidades Álbuns (até 31/12/2023)' = OURO 7 500 / PLATINA 15 000 / DIAMANTE 150 000, replaced by 'Unidades Álbuns (a partir de 01/01/2024)' = 3 500 / 7 000 / 70 000. SINGLES (per the four vigência rows of the current table): até semana 52/2023 — OURO 5 000, PLATINA 10 000, no Diamante; semana 01/2024 a 13/2025 — 5 000 / 10 000 / 100 000; semana 14/2025 a 26/2025 — 5 000 / 10 000 / 100 000 but with the new 103 stream ratio; a partir da semana 27/2025 — 12 000 / 25 000 / 250 000. Transitional rule Art. 24.2: streams accumulated on albums up to 31/12/2023 are multiplied by 0,5 when carried into the post-2024 rules. So a Portuguese album plaque awarded in 2018-2023 sits on 7 500/15 000 and one awarded from 2024 on 3 500/7 000; a single plaque before mid-2025 sits on 5 000/10 000.
countries.notes: ATTRIBUTION CAVEAT: the site credits these plaques to 'AFP'. AFP – Associação Fonográfica Portuguesa has no live site (afp.org.pt returns no DNS A record; www.afp.pt is the Associação Fiscal Portuguesa, a tax body, not the music one). The certifications themselves are defined and issued by Audiogest, which runs the joint 'TOP AFP/AUDIOGEST' charts: 'Galardões: certificações emitidas pela Audiogest'. The document read is therefore the issuing body's own regulation on its own domain. The live page https://www.audiogest.pt/regulamento-dos-servicos-de-monitorizacao-das-tabelas-de-vendas-top-audiogest-e-de-emissao-de-galardoes?lang=pt still links only the January 2024 version; the July-2025-amended PDF used here is the newer file on the same audiogest.pt domain (its Anexo III singles table carries the week-27/2025 row, which the Jan-2024 PDF does not). ELIGIBILITY: an Álbum needs total duration >= 25 minutes and >= 5 tracks (physical price >= EUR 5,95). YouTube streams are excluded from album Tops and album awards but count for singles/streams tables. Different versions of the same recording may be aggregated if title, essential lyric/recording and lead artist are unchanged. Award codes are formed as e.g. SG (Single) / LP or AL (Álbum) + sequential number + OU (Ouro) / PL (Platina) + year. The Direção may change the table at any time and new tables apply retroactively to past consumption.

countries.body: ARIA (Australian Recording Industry Association)
countries.sourceQuote: 'The current ARIA Accreditation levels are as follows: Singles — Gold: 35,000 units; Platinum: 70,000 units. Albums — Silver: 20,000 units; Gold: 35,000 units; Platinum: 70,000 units; Diamond: 500,000 units. Music Videos (including Audio Visual DVDs) — Gold: 7,500 units; Platinum: 15,000 units.' Corroborated verbatim in ARIA's own Code of Practice s.10.8(a): 'Singles and Albums — Gold 35,000 sales equivalent units; Platinum 70,000 sales equivalent units; Audiovisual — Gold 7,500; Platinum 15,000.'
countries.unitDefinition: 'Sales equivalent units' — sales plus converted streams. Code s.10.2: 'The physical product component for accreditations is based on net wholesale shipments to stores', which the member must aggregate with certified reports of '(i) sales from Digital Service Providers; and (ii) streams of Streaming Service Providers'. Streams are converted at 'the conversion rate applicable at the time that the streams occurred', using ARIA's own published calculator (https://www.aria.com.au/charts/accreditation-stream-calculator). Current factors in ARIA's Singles calculator, period 1 Sep 2025 to today: Subscription 200 (200 premium streams = 1 unit) and Ad Supported 445. ALBUMS (SEA): enter the aggregate streams of the tracks ranked 3 to 10 of the release, convert at the same period factors, scale by 10/8 to impute tracks 1 and 2, then divide by the 'Album track division factor: 10' — i.e. currently about 2,000 premium track streams per album unit. Only Australian streams of official (non-UGC) content the member has been paid for are eligible.
countries.multiplierRule: Literally N x the 70,000 Platinum threshold, and ARIA's Code proves it with its own worked example under s.10.10(b): a 500,000-selling album 'will now carry accreditation of a Diamond Award and 7 x Platinum. Some months later, having achieved a further 60,000 album sales and reached 560,000 sales, the Title will be eligible for additional Platinum accreditation. Its status will then be Diamond and 8 x Platinum.' (490,000 = 7x70,000; 560,000 = 8x70,000.) Multi-platinum must be claimed by the member on an application form; 'Additional seals will not be issued for multi-platinum achievements' (max 5 seals per release). No upper tier cap is published, so 19x Platinum = 1,330,000 units on ARIA's own arithmetic.
countries.diamondRule: A distinct, separate award — not Nx Platinum. Code s.10.10: 'The threshold for a Diamond Award is 500,000 sales within Australia. From 1 May 2024 ARIA Diamond Awards are based on Album sales only.' And s.10.10(b): 'The Diamond Award is considered a separate award. Thus, Platinum levels are maintained (and incremented as applicable) even if a Diamond Award has been awarded to a Title.' So a title can hold Diamond AND a running Platinum multiple simultaneously. Since 1 May 2024 Diamond cannot be awarded to a single, and the Diamond claim form is headed 'CLAIM FOR ACCREDITATION FOR DIAMOND AWARDS ... for the following Album' with Physical Sales / Digital Sales lines only (no stream line).
countries.changedSince2015: Gold/Platinum have not moved: 35,000/70,000 is stated as 'current' on both the accreditations page and the Code, and ARIA publishes no change date or previous value for them ('The introduction or amendment of accreditation levels will be at the discretion of the ARIA Board'). Everything else did move, all dated by ARIA: Diamond 'was introduced in 2015 to recognise significant achievement for Titles released from 1 July 2014'; from 1 May 2024 Diamond is album-sales-only; Silver was introduced for albums 'applicable to Titles released from 1 January 2021 only'; streams began counting toward singles from 1 July 2015; Stream Equivalent Albums from May 2017; separate premium vs ad-supported conversion factors from October 2018; official-content YouTube streams eligible for accreditation from March 2022. The conversion factors themselves are 'reviewed quarterly and adjusted as necessary' — ARIA's calculator lists every period, e.g. subscription 175 (Jul 2015), 185, 175, 200 (Oct 2018), 140 (Nov 2018), 170 (1 Sep 2023 through 31 Aug 2025), 200 (from 1 Sep 2025); ad-supported has ranged from 175 to 1,145 and is currently 445. So a 2018 plaque and a 2026 plaque at the same 70,000 units represent very different stream volumes.
countries.notes: Read at the body: https://www.aria.com.au/accreditations, plus ARIA's own Code of Practice PDF (https://content.aria.com.au/documents/aria-charts-code-24-august-2026.pdf, section 10 'ARIA ACCREDITATION AWARDS'), the Gold/Platinum claim form (footnote: 'Gold single/album 35,000: music video/DVD 7,500; Platinum single/album 70,000: music video/DVD 15,000'), the Diamond claim form, and the two official stream calculator spreadsheets on cdn.aria.com.au. SILVER IS ALBUM-ONLY AND HEAVILY CONDITIONED: 'Only awarded to albums by Australian artists', '20,000 unit threshold needs to be achieved within three years of the album's initial release', 'Only applicable to albums released after 1 January 2021', and only for product distributed by ARIA members — so a Burna Boy release could never hold an ARIA Silver. There is no Silver for singles and no Diamond for singles today. Extra category: Music Videos / Audiovisual DVDs at Gold 7,500 / Platinum 15,000. Accreditation is claim-based (a member's principal financial officer certifies the total), so absence of an ARIA plaque never means the threshold was not reached.

countries.body: IFPI Danmark
countries.unitDefinition: Sales + streaming, all converted to 'enheder' (units), with SEPARATE conversion factors for tracks and albums. Body's own wording: "Den aktuelle omregningsfaktor for henholdsvis tracks og album: Track: 1 stream = 1 enhed / 1 download = 100 enheder. Album: 1000 streams = 1 enhed / 1 download = 1 enhed." Also: "Både salg af fysiske eksemplarer, digitale downloadformater og streams tæller med." CRITICAL CONSEQUENCE: because 1 track stream = 1 unit, the TRACK thresholds are expressed in millions — Guld = 4,500,000 units, i.e. roughly 4.5 million streams. The album thresholds (10,000 / 20,000) are in album-equivalent units where 1,000 streams = 1 unit. Do not compare the two numbers as if they were the same currency. Conversion itself is done "efter M&I Services gældende regler" (IFPI DK's data supplier); IFPI DK states the ratios on its own page, which is what is quoted here. Promo giveaways excluded: "eksemplarer, der er foræret væk i salgsfremmende eller promotionsmæssige sammenhænge, medregnes ikke."
countries.multiplierRule: Literally N x the Platinum threshold. The body's own table lists Guld / Platin / Dobbelt Platin / Trippel Platin / 'o.s.v.' (etc.) with Album 10.000 / 20.000 / 40.000 / 60.000 and Track 4.500.000 / 9.000.000 / 18.000.000 / 27.000.000 — i.e. Dobbelt = 2x Platin, Trippel = 3x Platin, and the 'o.s.v.' column means the series continues linearly. IFPI DK's own live register (ifpi.dk/certificeringer-0) shows higher multiples written as '2xPlatin' and '4xPlatin', confirming the Nx-Platinum naming. So a 19x award in Denmark = 19 x 20,000 = 380,000 album units, or 19 x 9,000,000 = 171,000,000 track units.
countries.diamondRule: NO DIAMOND. IFPI Danmark does not award a Diamond certification. The criteria table has exactly four named columns — Guld, Platin, Dobbelt Platin, Trippel Platin — then 'o.s.v.'. The word 'diamant' does not appear on the criteria page or on the body's own certification register. Any Danish 'Diamond' claim is not from IFPI Danmark.
countries.changedSince2015: Current criteria are dated by the body itself: "Kriterierne for tildeling af guld- og platincertifikater er pr. 1. april 2016" (as of 1 April 2016). I verified against captures of IFPI Danmark's OWN page (web.archive.org captures of ifpi.dk/guld-platin) from 7 Nov 2018 and 5 Jan 2021: the thresholds AND the conversion factors are byte-for-byte identical to today. So nothing has moved anywhere inside the 2018-2026 plaque window — every DK plaque in that window was issued against 10,000/20,000 (album) and 4,500,000/9,000,000 (track). The body does not publish the pre-April-2016 values, so I report no prior figures. IFPI DK also notes the criteria are periodically adjusted ("Kriterierne justeres med mellemrum for at afspejle udviklingen i markedet").
countries.notes: Two categories only: 'Album' and 'Track' (there is no separate physical-single category — physical singles fold into Track on request: "Hvis producenten/distributøren ønsker at inkludere fysisk salg (singler)", the label must write in and supply documentation). No EP, no video, no streaming-only tier. IMPORTANT RULE FOR DATING PLAQUES: IFPI DK certifies against the criteria current at the time of certification, not at release — "Certificeringer sker altid efter de gældende kriterier, uanset hvornår udgivelsen er udgivet." Certificates are issued weekly and automatically from M&I Service data. SITE ACCESS NOTE: https://www.ifpi.dk fails TLS (certificate is for *.scannet.dk); the page is only reachable over http://www.ifpi.dk/guld-platin. It is readable and not bot-blocked.
countries.sourceQuote: Kriterierne for tildeling af guld- og platincertifikater er pr. 1. april 2016: Album (Fysisk + digital + streaming) Guld 10.000, Platin 20.000, Dobbelt Platin 40.000, Trippel Platin 60.000, ... ; Track (Fysisk + digital + streaming) Guld 4.500.000, Platin 9.000.000, Dobbelt Platin 18.000.000, Trippel Platin 27.000.000, ... ; Track: 1 stream = 1 enhed, 1 download = 100 enheder; Album: 1000 streams = 1 enhed, 1 download = 1 enhed.

countries.body: Pro-Música Brasil (Pró-Música Brasil Produtores Fonográficos Associados)
countries.unitDefinition: READ THE FIRST LINE OF notes BEFORE USING THESE INTEGERS — Brazil publishes two different tables and the integers here are the NACIONAL one. Units are a multi-metric consumption sum, not pure sales. Body's own wording on the table: "Unidades necessárias para emissão de certificados de vendas são baseadas num sistema de consumo de música multimétrico, que considera a soma de vendas físicas, downloads e streaming de áudio e vídeo de um mesmo produto. Aplica-se fatores de conversão de modo a permitir a equivalência entre estes diferentes modelos de negócio..." And on the CERTIFICADOS page: "A certificação de vendas leva em consideração todos os formatos de consumo... ponderado com base no valor relativo de cada métodos de consumo de acordo com a metodologia TEA (track equivalente álbum), adotado internacionalmente com fatores de conversão de streaming/download/vendas físicas revisados periodicamente." Pro-Música does not state a bare 'N streams = 1 unit' ratio, but it publishes the equivalent stream totals per tier, from which the ratio is exact arithmetic on its own numbers: SINGLES 200 audio streams = 1 unit and 1,000 video streams = 1 unit (40,000 units <-> 8,000,000 audio <-> 40,000,000 video). ALBUMS 2,000 audio streams = 1 unit and 10,000 video streams = 1 unit (40,000 units <-> 80,000,000 audio <-> 400,000,000 video). Same ratios hold on the international table. Note the unit COUNTS are identical for singles and albums (40,000 / 80,000 / 300,000) — only the stream equivalents differ.
countries.multiplierRule: Two separate ladders, and only Platinum is a plain multiple. Platina Duplo = 2x Platina (160,000) and Platina Triplo = 3x Platina (240,000). But Diamante starts a NEW base: Diamante Duplo = 2x Diamante (600,000), Diamante Triplo = 3x Diamante (900,000). So an 'Nx' Brazilian award means N times whichever base tier it names, and a 3x Platinum (240,000) is far below a plain Diamond (300,000). The published table stops at Triplo, but Pro-Música's own certificate register carries higher multiples — its award-type filter includes 'Diamante Triplo' and 'Diamante Sêxtuplo' (6x) — so the series continues linearly beyond what the table prints. For a high award such as 19x, the body publishes no printed value; compute as 19 x the named base (19 x 80,000 platinum, or 19 x 300,000 diamond) and flag it as extrapolated from the ladder rather than quoted.
countries.diamondRule: DIAMOND IS A DISTINCT THRESHOLD, NOT A MULTIPLE OF PLATINUM. Nacional Diamante = 300,000 units (7.5x Ouro, 3.75x Platina). Internacional Diamante = 160,000 units (8x Ouro, 4x Platina). It sits above Platina Triplo (240,000 nacional / 120,000 internacional) and then spawns its own Duplo/Triplo/Sêxtuplo ladder. Brazil actively awards it — the live register returns Diamante certificates.
countries.changedSince2015: CANNOT BE EVIDENCED FROM THE BODY — treat older Brazilian plaques with caution. The table carries no effective date and no 'a partir de' anywhere, and Pro-Música publishes no dated announcement of a threshold change that I could find on its own site. The only archived captures of the body's own table page start 23 June 2026 (the table page appears not to have been crawled before that); the 23 Jun 2026 capture matches today's values exactly, so nothing has moved in the last few months. Everything earlier is unevidenced at the body. The CERTIFICADOS page does say the conversion factors are "revisados periodicamente", so a 2018-2020 Brazilian plaque should NOT be assumed to have been issued against these numbers. If a plaque's tier matters, date it from the certificate, not from this table.
countries.notes: CRITICAL — BRAZIL PUBLISHES TWO TABLES AND THE INTEGERS IN THIS RECORD ARE THE 'NACIONAL' ONE. Non-Brazilian repertoire (which is what every Burna Boy / Afrobeats plaque is) is certified on the 'INTERNACIONAL' table at exactly HALF: SINGLES INTERNACIONAL — Ouro 20,000 (4,000,000 audio streams / 20,000,000 video), Platina 40,000, Platina Duplo 80,000, Platina Triplo 120,000, Diamante 160,000, Diamante Duplo 320,000, Diamante Triplo 480,000. ÁLBUNS INTERNACIONAL — Ouro 20,000 (40,000,000 audio / 200,000,000 video), Platina 40,000, Platina Duplo 80,000, Platina Triplo 120,000, Diamante 160,000, Diamante Duplo 320,000, Diamante Triplo 480,000. If you are pricing this site's plaques, the international column is the one that applies. EXTRA CATEGORY: DVD is certified separately on PHYSICAL SALES ONLY ("Considera apenas vendas no formato físico") — DVD Nacional Ouro 25,000 / Platina 50,000 / Platina Duplo 100,000 / Platina Triplo 150,000 / Diamante 250,000 / Diamante Duplo 500,000 / Diamante Triplo 750,000; DVD Internacional Ouro 15,000 / Platina 30,000 / Platina Duplo 60,000 / Platina Triplo 90,000 / Diamante 125,000 / Diamante Duplo 250,000 / Diamante Triplo 375,000. No EP tier, no streaming-only tier, no Prata (Silver) — the word does not occur on the table or the register. DUPLICATE PAGE: the body hosts an identical second copy at .../tabela-de-niveis-de-certificacao-pro-musica-2/ (titled 'NOVA'); I diffed both and every number matches, so the '-2' page is not a newer schedule. The CERTIFICADOS page links the non-'-2' URL as the "Tabela de Níveis de Certificação atualizada", which is why I cite that one. Certificates are issued only on a label's request ("mediante solicitação das gravadoras associadas"), so absence from the register is not evidence of non-certification.
countries.sourceQuote: SINGLES – NACIONAL: Ouro 40.000 (8.000.000 streams de áudio / 40.000.000 streams de vídeo); Platina 80.000; Platina Duplo 160.000; Platina Triplo 240.000; Diamante 300.000; Diamante Duplo 600.000; Diamante Triplo 900.000. ÁLBUNS – NACIONAL: Ouro 40.000 (80.000.000 áudio / 400.000.000 vídeo); Platina 80.000; Platina Duplo 160.000; Platina Triplo 240.000; Diamante 300.000; Diamante Duplo 600.000; Diamante Triplo 900.000. SINGLES – INTERNACIONAL: Ouro 20.000; Platina 40.000; Platina Duplo 80.000; Platina Triplo 120.000; Diamante 160.000. ÁLBUNS – INTERNACIONAL: Ouro 20.000; Platina 40.000; Platina Duplo 80.000; Platina Triplo 120.000; Diamante 160.000. "Unidades necessárias para emissão de certificados de vendas são baseadas num sistema de consumo de música multimétrico, que considera a soma de vendas físicas, downloads e streaming de áudio e vídeo de um mesmo produto."

countries.body: Promusicae (Productores de Música de España), publishing through its own portal El Portal de Música (EPDM)
countries.unitDefinition: Sales OR streaming equivalent, in a single 'unidades' currency — the body's exact phrase is "las unidades (vendidas o equivalente en escucha)" (English version: "the units (sold or streaming equivalent)"). THE CONVERSION RATIO IS NOT PUBLISHED. Neither promusicae.es nor elportaldemusica.es states how many streams make a unit, and promusicae.es has no certification-rules or methodology page at all (www.promusicae.es/certificaciones/ returns 404; the site's nav carries only quienes-somos, socios, listas, informes, noticias). I found no official PDF stating a ratio. So I return no ratio rather than importing one from a chart blog. Do not infer the ratio by dividing an old streaming-chart figure into a threshold — Promusicae's 2013-era streaming-chart award (a separate scheme) is not the current unit conversion.
countries.multiplierRule: N x the named base award. Promusicae's own award register offers exactly two award types in its filter (values 'gold' and 'platinum') and renders each certificate with a multiplier glyph — '1 ×', '2 ×', '3 ×' — and its charts show up to '10x' for current albums. So a 3x Platinum album = 3 x 40,000 = 120,000 units and a 19x would be 19 x 40,000 = 760,000 units (songs: 19 x 100,000 = 1,900,000). CAVEAT WORTH CARRYING: Promusicae states the base thresholds in prose but never spells out the multiplier arithmetic in words anywhere on its site; the linear reading is taken from its own register's 'N ×' notation over gold/platinum only. Treat the arithmetic as inferred-from-the-body's-own-register, not quoted.
countries.diamondRule: NO DIAMOND. Promusicae awards only Disco de Oro and Disco de Platino — both are its registered trademarks ("Disco de Oro® y Disco de Platino® son marcas registradas de PROMUSICAE"). Its awards register exposes exactly two award values, 'gold' and 'platinum'; the string 'diamante' appears on the page only inside artist names (JC EL DIAMANTE, OMAR MONTES / JC EL DIAMANTE). A Spanish 'Diamond' does not exist at this body.
countries.changedSince2015: YES — SONGS CHANGED IN APRIL 2025 AND THIS BREAKS OLDER SPANISH SINGLE PLAQUES. Albums have held at Oro 20,000 / Platino 40,000 throughout every capture I checked. Songs moved from Oro 30,000 / Platino 60,000 to Oro 50,000 / Platino 100,000 between 4 April 2025 and 1 May 2025 — narrowed on captures of PROMUSICAE'S OWN EPDM page: 4 Jan 2025, 5 Mar 2025, 1 Apr 2025 and 4 Apr 2025 all read "Canciones: disco de oro 30.000, disco de platino: 60.000"; 1 May 2025, 20 May 2025, 1 Jun 2025 and every capture since read "Singles: Gold 50,000. Platinum: 100,000". Promusicae published no dated announcement of the change — the values simply changed on the page — so the April 2025 bracket is evidenced by archived copies of the body's own page, not by a body statement. Anything before Jan 2025 (i.e. whether songs were 30,000/60,000 for the whole 2018-2024 window, or lower earlier) is NOT evidenced at the body and I am not asserting it. PRACTICAL CONSEQUENCE: a Spanish single plaque awarded 2018-2024 was NOT awarded against 50,000 units. Do not describe an old ES single certification as '50,000 units'.
countries.notes: SOURCING NOTE: promusicae.es itself publishes no threshold page. The only place PROMUSICAE states its current thresholds is the awards page of El Portal de Música, which is PROMUSICAE's own site — its legal notice reads "La utilización de la web www.elportaldemusica.es, así como de los servicios que se ofrecen en la misma por PROMUSICAE..." and the footer is "2026 © PROMUSICAE". So this satisfies the own-site rule; it is not a third-party chart site. CATEGORIES: the register's group filter has four — CANCIONES (songs), ALBUMES, SINGLES (legacy physical singles, historic only) and DVD. Promusicae publishes thresholds for only ALBUMES and CANCIONES; it states no criteria for DVD or for the legacy SINGLES category, so those are null-by-absence, not zero. The register goes back to 1994 and holds 16,260 certificates. Certification is cumulative and, per Promusicae's 2023 announcement, the awards history is now browsable at EPDM.
countries.sourceQuote: En la actualidad, las unidades (vendidas o equivalente en escucha) necesarias para cada certificación son: Álbumes: disco de oro: 20.000, disco de platino: 40.000. Canciones: disco de oro 50.000, disco de platino: 100.000. [English version on the same page: "At present, the units (sold or streaming equivalent) required for each certification are: Albums: Gold: 20,000, Platinum: 40,000. Singles: Gold 50,000. Platinum: 100,000."]

countries.body: NVPI (Nederlandse Vereniging van Producenten en Importeurs van beeld- en geluidsdragers) — NVPI Muziek/Audio, which runs the official certification register at goudplatina.nl
countries.unitDefinition: The unit IS a stream, not a sale. NVPI counts Dutch streams only and converts sales INTO streams (the reverse of most bodies). Own wording: 'Zowel betaalde streams als ad-supported streams van alle bekende audio-streamingdiensten waaronder bijvoorbeeld Spotify, Deezer en Apple Music. Elke digitale (download) of fysieke (lp, cd) verkoop telt ook mee. Één albumverkoop staat gelijk aan 2150 streams, één singleverkoop staat gelijk aan 215 streams.' Excluded: 'Streams en verkopen buiten Nederland' and 'Streams bij gratis videodiensten zoals YouTube, of streams op socials media platforms zoals Instagram of TikTok.' The regulation PDF adds that for singles only single downloads count (not album downloads), and for albums only whole-album downloads and physical sales count, and physical only 'mits verkocht middels een officiële verkooppartij die data aanlevert bij GfK'.
countries.multiplierRule: There is NO multiplier tier any more. NVPI's own news page states: 'Meervoudig Platina bestaat sinds dit jaar niet meer. Daarvoor is Diamant in de plaats gekomen.' (published 19-02-2024, i.e. abolished as of 1 January 2024). The current Reglement Goud/Platina/Diamant 2025 defines only three levels — Goud, Platina, Diamant — and no 2x/3x/Nx rule. Meervoudig Platina DID exist for pre-2024 Dutch plaques, but NVPI no longer publishes anywhere what its thresholds were, so any pre-2024 Dutch multi-platinum award cannot be priced from an NVPI source. Do not assume Nx Platina.
countries.diamondRule: Diamant is a DISTINCT threshold, not a multiple of Platina. Single Diamant = 50,000,000 streams (2.5x the 20M Platina level); Album Diamant = 200,000,000 streams (2.5x the 80M Platina level). NVPI: 'De diamanten status bestaat sinds 1 januari 2024 en wordt toegekend aan singles die in Nederland 50 miljoen streams halen en albums die 200 miljoen keer gestreamd worden.' The Netherlands DOES award Diamond — first ever went to FLEMMING on 19 February 2024.
countries.changedSince2015: Yes — one confirmed change inside the window, dated by NVPI itself to 1 January 2024. The reglement and the public info page both head the table 'Per 1 januari 2024 gelden de volgende benodigde aantallen'. Three things changed on that date per NVPI's own news item of 19-02-2024: (a) the required amounts were reset, (b) Diamant was introduced ('De diamanten status bestaat sinds 1 januari 2024'), and (c) Meervoudig Platina was abolished. CRITICAL GAP: NVPI does NOT publish the pre-2024 values. Its older regulation PDFs are 404 on nvpi.nl (e.g. /app/uploads/sites/3/2020/01/Aanvraagformulier-penningen-met-reglement-2020_Deel2.pdf returns 404), and neither goudplatina.nl nor nvpi.nl states the old numbers anywhere. So for the 2018–2023 Dutch plaques on this site, the threshold in force at award time is NOT sourceable at the body and must be left null rather than back-filled. One further, smaller change: the 2025 reglement (ReglementGoud-Platina-Diamant2025.pdf) adds a clause absent from the 2024 reglement — 'Voor de genres jazz en klassiek zijn 50% van de hierboven genoemde aantallen nodig voor certificering.' The 2024 and 2025 reglements are otherwise numerically identical.
countries.sourceQuote: Per 1 januari 2024 gelden de volgende benodigde aantallen: Singles — Goud: 10 miljoen streams / Platina: 20 miljoen streams / Diamant: 50 miljoen streams. Albums — Goud: 40 miljoen streams / Platina: 80 miljoen streams / Diamant: 200 miljoen streams. … Één albumverkoop staat gelijk aan 2150 streams, één singleverkoop staat gelijk aan 215 streams.
countries.notes: Everything above was read at the body. Pages actually read: https://www.goudplatina.nl/informatie (NVPI's official certification site — 'De officiële status van Goud, Platina of Diamant is door leden van NVPI Muziek aan te vragen bij het secretariaat van NVPI'), NVPI's own regulation PDF https://goudplatina.cdn.prismic.io/goudplatina/Z2WriJbqstJ98vo5_ReglementGoud-Platina-Diamant2025.pdf (and the 2024 edition, Ztri67zzk9ZrXGEm), and NVPI's news page https://www.nvpi.nl/nieuws/7252/eerste-diamanten-status-ooit-is-voor-flemming (source of the multiple-platinum abolition). Other rules from the reglement: singles are certified per title/per master and 'Streams van remixen, covers en alternatieve versies worden gezien als verschillende titels en mogen hier niet bij opgeteld worden'; an album 'dient ten minste 5 individuele masters te bevatten'; for albums 'Streams van masters die ook op een eerder uitgebracht album staan tellen niet mee'; 'Zowel bij singles als albums is de data en meetwijze van NVPI bepalend voor certificering.' Only two award types exist in the register (Type: Single / Type: Album) — no EP, video or streaming-single category. Beware a false friend: NVPI has a 'Zilveren Fonograaf' in its site menu, but that is an industry honour, not a sales certification tier; there is no Zilver plaque.

countries.body: Ifpi Sverige (the former GLF, Grammofonleverantörernas förening) — 'Guld- och Platinacertifikat delas ut av Ifpi Sverige.'
countries.unitDefinition: The two categories are measured in different things. SONG ('Låt'): pure streams, no sales at all — 'Enbart streams får räknas in till Guld- och Platina för Låt', and since 1 Jan 2018 'Fysiska singlar och downloads räknas inte längre in.' Streams are capped, not raw: 'Antalet streams baseras på s k cappade streams, dvs det finns ett tak på hur många lyssningar per låt per dag per användare som räknas med. Detta "tak" kan förändras över tid utan att detta meddelas vid varje enskilt tillfälle.' Ifpi Sverige deliberately does not publish the cap's value. Music-video streams count only under conditions: 'För att musikvideostreams skall omfattas av certifiering skall lyssnandet/tittandet ske i ett inloggat läge. Vidare får endast officiella musikvideos på YouTube omfattas.' ALBUM: sales+streaming units — physical sales can be added to streams ('för album kan fysisk försäljning adderas till streams'), and album streams are likewise capped streams. The stream-to-unit CONVERSION RATIO for albums is not published anywhere on ifpi.se — the calculator that applies it is a members-only tool ('ett verktyg som är tillgängligt via ifpi.se', hosted at sys.ifpi.se, which is not publicly reachable). So the album ratio is null, not assumed.
countries.multiplierRule: NOT PUBLISHED. Ifpi Sverige publishes exactly two levels, Guld and Platina, in its only threshold table. No 2x/3x/Nx definition appears on the site, in the Guld- och Platina-guide 2024 PDF, or in any news post; a site search for 'multiplatina' returns only the Guld- och Platina page itself. The one document behind that page's 'Ansökan om multiplatina' link is a DIFFERENT scheme — the IFPI international Multi Platinum Award form (https://www.ifpi.se/wp-content/uploads/2017/01/Multi_platinum_application_Sweden.pdf), whose own notes read: 'This form refers to Multi Platinum (minimum 1 million sales/units) award applications for sales worldwide of CD albums from Swedish Artists' and 'Sales of physical product (albums) including digital sales are eligible, singles are not.' That is a worldwide 1,000,000-unit album award for Swedish artists, NOT a Swedish domestic Nx-platinum rule, and must not be used to price a Swedish 2x/3x plaque.
countries.diamondRule: Ifpi Sverige does not award Diamond. The published format table contains only Guld and Platina columns, and a site search for 'diamant' on ifpi.se returns 'Inget hittades. Inget matchade dina söktermer.' Any 'Diamond (Sweden)' claim has no basis at the body. (Note: a Swedish music blog circulates a '12 million streams = Diamant' figure; that is not Ifpi Sverige's — 12,000,000 is Ifpi Sverige's PLATINA level for a song. Do not carry it over.)
countries.changedSince2015: Yes — twice, both dated by Ifpi Sverige. (1) 1 January 2018, announced 6 February 2018 in 'Nya nivåer för Guld och Platina': 'Fysiska singlar och downloads räknas inte längre in. Nuvarande specialregler för releaser under perioden 1 juli 2004 – 31 december 2009 slopas. Beräkningsgrunden för album behålls som som idag men gränserna sänks till 15 000 för Guld och 30 000 för Platina (för album kan fysisk försäljning adderas till streams).' So the ALBUM thresholds have been 15,000/30,000 since 1 Jan 2018 and are unchanged today — that covers the whole 2018–2026 plaque window. The guide PDF confirms the song rule start date: 'Från och med den 1 januari 2018 räknas endast streaming med i beräkningen för guld och platina.' (2) 1 January 2024: 'Från och med den 1 januari 2024 gäller nya regler för beräkning av Guld- och Platinacertifiering', which produced today's song levels of 6,000,000/12,000,000. CRITICAL GAP: Ifpi Sverige does not publish the PRE-2024 song thresholds. There is no news post giving them (site searches for 'certifiering', 'nya regler', 'guld platina' surface only the 2018 item), and the 2024 guide states only the post-change table. Equally important for dating plaques, the body itself warns on the live page: 'observera att beroende på releasedatum kan andra gränser gälla' — other limits may apply depending on release date. So a Swedish song plaque awarded before 2024 cannot be priced from the current 6M/12M figures, and the correct pre-2024 number is not sourceable at the body.
countries.sourceQuote: Så här ser gränserna ut för Guld- och Platina vid digital försäljning (observera att beroende på releasedatum kan andra gränser gälla). *Enbart streams får räknas in till Guld- och Platina för Låt. Format / Guld / Platina — Låt (enbart streams) 6 000 000* / 12 000 000*; Album 15 000 / 30 000; Musik DVD 5 000 / 10 000; Folkmusik 10 000 / 20 000; Jazz 10 000 / 20 000; Klassiskt 10 000 / 20 000; Barn 10 000 / 20 000.
countries.unreadableReason: Three specific values are null because Ifpi Sverige does not publish them, not because the site was unreachable (ifpi.se was fully readable). (a) Diamond, album and single: the body has no Diamond tier at all — its format table has only Guld and Platina, and an on-site search for 'diamant' returns 'Inget hittades'. (b) Silver, album and single: same — no Silver tier, on-site search for 'silver' returns 'Inget hittades'. (c) Additionally unsourceable, though not fields above: the album stream-to-unit conversion ratio (the calculator applying it is behind a member login at sys.ifpi.se, which did not resolve), the pre-2024 song thresholds, and any domestic Nx-platinum rule.
countries.notes: Pages actually read at the body: https://www.ifpi.se/musikbolag/guld-och-platina/ (the threshold table), https://www.ifpi.se/wp-content/uploads/2024/03/Guld-och-Platina-guide-2024.pdf ('Guide för Guld- och platinacertifiering'), https://www.ifpi.se/2018/02/06/nya-nivaer-guld-och-platina/ (the 2018 change), and the multi-platinum form PDF. Ifpi Sverige uses MORE categories than album/single, and they are separate thresholds, all read off the same table: Musik DVD 5,000 Guld / 10,000 Platina; Folkmusik 10,000/20,000; Jazz 10,000/20,000; Klassiskt 10,000/20,000; Barn 10,000/20,000. The genre categories are a genuine alternative album threshold, so a Swedish jazz or children's album plaque is a 10,000/20,000 award, not 15,000/30,000. Eligibility limits worth knowing when dating plaques: 'Endast masterägare kan ansöka om Guld- och Platinacertifikat (dvs den som äger inspelningen)' and 'Endast album släppta från och med 1 januari 2010 kan ansöka om guld eller platinacertifikat.' The song rules 'gäller oavsett låtens/inspelningens releasedatum' — i.e. the streaming-only basis applies regardless of when the song came out, which is the opposite of the album rule.

countries.body: FIMI (Federazione Industria Musicale Italiana), with sales measurement by NIQ (formerly GfK) — 'Dal gennaio 2009 FIMI in collaborazione con NIQ … ufficializza le certificazioni di vendita di ogni singola registrazione musicale pubblicata e venduta in Italia.'
countries.unitDefinition: Sales + streaming equivalents, in 'unità', and the two categories convert at different rates. The certifications page heads the table: 'FIMI e GfK riconoscono le seguenti soglie di certificazione (fisico, download e streaming)'. SINGLES (Nota metodologica): '1 download digitale = 165 ascolti in streaming premium e 715 ascolti ad-supported' — so 165 premium streams = 1 unit, 715 ad-supported streams = 1 unit. ALBUMS use the Nordic Sea Model: track streams are summed with the top track capped at 70% of the album's total ('si escludono gli ascolti del primo brano più ascoltato che eccedono il 70% del totale streams dell'album stesso'), then 'Conversion rate premium: il numero totale degli ascolti premium (con cap del 70% sul brano più ascoltato) viene diviso per 1.650' and 'Conversion rate ad-supported: … viene diviso per 7.150' — i.e. the singles rate multiplied by an Equivalent Album Track of 10. Exclusions: 'Sono escluse le tracce streaming con durata inferiore a 30 secondi e gli streaming via radio', plus a per-user daily listening cap set by each platform, and only 'ufficiali' content (uploaded to the artist's or label's official channel) — user-generated content is excluded.
countries.multiplierRule: Literally N times the Platinum threshold, published as an explicit ladder rather than left to inference. Albums: platino 50,000; 2° platino 100,000; 3° 150,000; 4° 200,000; 5° 250,000; 6° 300,000; 7° 350,000; 8° 400,000; 9° 450,000 — each 'Oltre' N x 50,000. Singles: platino 200,000; 2° 400,000; 3° 600,000; 4° 800,000; 5° 1,000,000; 6° 1,200,000; 7° 1,400,000; 8° 1,600,000; 9° 1,800,000 — each N x 200,000. PRICING TRAP: because the multiples are defined off the Platinum threshold and that threshold has been raised twice since 2018, a given Nx plaque means different unit counts at different dates. A 3x Platino single awarded in 2018 was 210,000 units (3 x 70,000); the same 3x Platino awarded in 2026 is 600,000 units (3 x 200,000). The published ladder stops at 9° platino followed by diamante 1°; FIMI publishes NO threshold above diamante, so an Italian award beyond that (a 10x-19x claim) has no value sourceable at the body.
countries.diamondRule: Italy does award Diamante, and it is a named tier with its own row — but numerically it is exactly 10x the Platinum threshold, and it rescales whenever Platinum moves. Currently: albums 'diamante 1° Oltre 500.000' (10 x 50,000) and singles 'diamante 1° Oltre 2.000.000' (10 x 200,000). That it scales rather than being a fixed number is confirmed by FIMI's own 2019 blog post, where singles Platino was 70,000 and the same ladder read 'DIAMANTE, oltre le 700.000 copie vendute' — again exactly 10x. It sits above 9° platino, so it is the top published tier, and FIMI numbers it '1°' but publishes no 2° diamante threshold.
countries.changedSince2015: Yes, for SINGLES only — three times, each announced by FIMI itself, and albums never moved. (1) From week 01/2020, announced 18/12/2019 in 'Novità sul fronte delle classifiche di vendita FIMI/GfK': 'le soglie per l'attribuzione delle certificazioni dei Singoli ORO e PLATINO … passerà dagli attuali 25.000 e 50.000 a, rispettivamente, 35.000 e 70.000. Nessun cambiamento interverrà invece sulle soglie degli Album, che rimarranno 25.000 per l'oro e 50.000 per il platino.' (2) From week 01/2022, announced 26/10/2021: 'a partire dalla week 01/2022 si passerà dalle attuali 35.000 e 70.000 copie vendute per i singoli ORO e PLATINO a, rispettivamente, 50.000 e 100.000. Nessun cambiamento interverrà invece sulle soglie di Album & Compilation, che rimarranno 25.000 per l'oro e 50.000 per il platino.' (3) From week 01/2025, announced 16/12/2024: 'i nuovi parametri FIMI/GfK saranno infatti di 100.000 unità vendute per l'ORO e di 200.000 unità vendute per il PLATINO … Nessun cambiamento interverrà invece sulle soglie di Album & Compilation, che rimarranno 25.000 per l'ORO e 50.000 per il PLATINO.' So the singles timeline across the 2018–2026 plaque window is: 25,000/50,000 through 2019 → 35,000/70,000 for 2020–2021 → 50,000/100,000 for 2022–2024 → 100,000/200,000 from 2025. Albums and compilations have been 25,000/50,000 the entire time, confirmed in all three announcements. A single also changed in the same 2019 announcement: from week 01/2020 compilation sales are counted inside the album chart.
countries.sourceQuote: Alla luce delle nuove condizioni di mercato FIMI e GfK riconoscono le seguenti soglie di certificazione (fisico, download e streaming). Album: oro 1° Oltre 25.000; platino 1° Oltre 50.000; 2° platino Oltre 100.000; 3° Oltre 150.000; 4° Oltre 200.000; 5° Oltre 250.000; 6° Oltre 300.000; 7° Oltre 350.000; 8° Oltre 400.000; 9° Oltre 450.000; diamante 1° Oltre 500.000. Singoli: oro 1° Oltre 100.000; platino 1° Oltre 200.000; 2° platino Oltre 400.000; 3° Oltre 600.000; 4° Oltre 800.000; 5° Oltre 1.000.000; 6° Oltre 1.200.000; 7° Oltre 1.400.000; 8° Oltre 1.600.000; 9° Oltre 1.800.000; diamante 1° Oltre 2.000.000.
countries.notes: Pages actually read at the body: https://www.fimi.it/top-of-the-music/certificazioni/ (the live ladder), https://www.fimi.it/top-of-the-music/nota-metodologica/ (unit definitions and stream conversion), and three FIMI announcements for the change history — https://www.fimi.it/news/novita-sul-fronte-delle-classifiche-di-vendita-fimi-gfk/ (18/12/2019), https://www.fimi.it/news/certificazioni-singoli-fimi-gfk-nuove-soglie-di-vendita-a-partire-dal-2022/ (26/10/2021), https://www.fimi.it/news/certificazioni-singoli-fimi-gfk-nuove-soglie-di-vendita-a-partire-dal-2025/ (16/12/2024), plus https://www.fimi.it/blog/grandi-successi-da-milioni-di-copie-nei-decenni-passati-ma-solo-adesso-conquistano-le-certificazioni-fimi-perche/ (15/04/2019) which pins the pre-2020 ladder including diamante at 700,000. Note every threshold is stated as 'Oltre' (above) N, so the value is a floor to exceed, not to reach. FIMI's certification sections are 'Album e Compilation' and 'Singoli Online' — compilations share the album thresholds, and there is no separate EP, video or streaming-single certification. An 'album' needs 6 or more tracks ('Possono essere considerati ALBUM solo i supporti che hanno 6 o più tracce'), with a sub-6-track exception on label notification if it runs over 25 minutes; anything smaller is grouped into Singoli. Where a track sits on two albums, its streams go to the most recently released one; where a track is credited to several artists, the streams count for the first-named 'Artista principale'. FIMI's own explanation for old catalogue titles being certified only recently: sales count only from the start of FIMI/GfK measurement in 2010, so an Italian plaque never reflects pre-2010 sales. The site carries an explicit anti-AI-crawling notice, which does not affect the readability of the published thresholds.

countries.body: ZPAV (Związek Producentów Audio-Video)
countries.unitDefinition: SPLIT SYSTEM — albums are in UNITS, singles are in PLN REVENUE, not units. Albums: "Wyróżnienia przyznawane są wg liczby sprzedanych pakietów" (packages sold; a multi-disc set counts as 1). Physical + digital are summed. Vinyl is multiplied: "liczba sztuk sprzedanych nośników winylowych mnożona jest przez 2,5" (from 24 Feb 2017). Digital album conversion is REVENUE-based: "sprzedaż jednego albumu jest równoznaczna z uzyskaniem przychodu 35 zł z tytułu pobrań cyfrowych któregokolwiek z tytułów albumu ... i/lub przychód przypisany z tytułu streamingu" — i.e. 35 PLN of net download+streaming revenue across all the album's tracks = 1 album unit. Legacy fallback for digital sales made before 1 March 2017 only: "suma 10 płatnych pobrań ... lub 2500 szt. streamów ... jest równoznaczne ze sprzedażą 1 albumu". SINGLES ARE NOT COUNTED IN UNITS AT ALL: the thresholds are gross PLN revenue — "Przy przyznawaniu poszczególnych wyróżnień dla singli obowiązują następujące poziomy sprzedaży cyfrowej (progi wartości w PLN)". The integers reported in singleGold/singlePlatinum/singleDiamond are ZŁOTY, NOT UNITS, and are not comparable with unit thresholds in any other country. Legacy fallback for pre-1 March 2017 digital only: "jedno płatne pobranie singla ... lub 250 szt. streamów ... jest równoznaczne ze sprzedażą 1 singla". Physical singles are excluded entirely: "Sprzedaż singli w postaci fizycznej nie jest brana pod uwagę."
countries.multiplierRule: ZPAV does NOT use an open-ended Nx multiplier — it publishes a fixed, explicitly enumerated ladder that stops at 3x, and the named tiers are literal multiples of the Platinum/Diamond base. Albums (muzyka rozrywkowa): Złota 15 000, Platynowa 30 000, Podwójna Platynowa 60 000 (2x Platinum), Potrójna Platynowa 90 000 (3x Platinum), then Diamentowa 150 000, Podwójna Diamentowa 300 000 (2x Diamond), Potrójna Diamentowa 450 000 (3x Diamond). Singles (PLN): 125 000 / 250 000 / 500 000 / 750 000 / 1 000 000 / 2 000 000 / 3 000 000 on the same ladder. The published table ends at Potrójna Diamentowa; ZPAV states no tier above 3x Diamond, so any Polish award above that is not provided for in the current regulation. The superseded regulation did state an open Platinum multiplier: "Za wielokrotność ilości sprzedaży wymaganej do otrzymania Platynowej Płyty przyznawana jest kolejna Platynowa Płyta (Podwójna Platynowa Płyta, Potrójna Platynowa Płyta, Poczwórna Platynowa Płyta)."
countries.diamondRule: Diamond IS a distinct, separately published threshold — not an Nx multiple of Platinum. For albums (muzyka rozrywkowa) Diamentowa Płyta = 150 000 units, which is 5x the 30 000 Platinum level, and for singles Diamentowa = 1 000 000 zł, which is 4x the 250 000 zł Platinum level. Because the two ratios differ, Diamond cannot be derived from Platinum — it is its own row in ZPAV's table. Poland does award Diamond routinely, and also Podwójna/Potrójna Diamentowa (2x and 3x the Diamond figure).
countries.changedSince2015: YES — a major change, and it lands squarely inside the 2018-2026 plaque window. The current regulation is titled "REGULAMIN PRZYZNAWANIA WYRÓŻNIEŃ ZŁOTYCH, PLATYNOWYCH I DIAMENTOWYCH PŁYT (od stycznia 2025)" and closes "Niniejszy Regulamin obowiązuje od 1 stycznia 2025." ZPAV publishes the superseded regulation on the same page ("do końca 2024", in force from 01.08.2021), so the previous values are stated by the body itself. THE SINGLE BIGGEST TRAP: the pre-2025 album table split entertainment music by repertoire origin, and FOREIGN repertoire had LOWER thresholds — "rozrywka - rep. zagraniczny" Gold 10 000 / Platinum 20 000 / Diamond 100 000, versus "rozrywka - rep. krajowy" 15 000 / 30 000 / 150 000. The 2025 regulation abolished the domestic/foreign split, so a single "muzyka rozrywkowa" band of 15 000 / 30 000 / 150 000 now covers everyone. Consequence: a Polish album plaque awarded to a non-Polish artist in 2018-2024 was earned at 10 000 (Gold) / 20 000 (Platinum) / 100 000 (Diamond), while the same plaque awarded from 1 Jan 2025 required 15 000 / 30 000 / 150 000 — a 50% jump. Singles moved even harder: old digital-single thresholds were "25 000 / 50 000 zł" (Gold), "50 000 / 100 000 zł" (Platinum), "250 000 / 500 000 zł" (Diamond) on a units-OR-revenue basis; the new regulation drops units entirely and sets pure revenue at 125 000 / 250 000 / 1 000 000 zł — Gold went from 50 000 zł to 125 000 zł (2.5x) and Diamond from 500 000 zł to 1 000 000 zł (2x). The digital-album conversion rate also worsened, from "Wartość przychodu 20 zł ... jest równoznaczny ze sprzedażą 1 albumu" (in force from 01.03.2017) to 35 zł per album unit from 2025. The vinyl x2.5 multiplier dates from 24 Feb 2017. Older video-album categories (ALBUMY VIDEO: rozrywka 5 000 / 10 000 / 50 000; muzyka poważna and jazz 2 500 / 5 000 / 25 000) existed under the pre-2025 rules and are gone from the current one.
countries.notes: ROUTE TO SOURCE: zpav.pl itself carries no certification page — its top menu links out to https://www.olis.pl (labelled "ZPAV - Bestsellery i Wyróżnienia"), and OLiS is ZPAV's own official chart-and-awards service (footer: "© ZPAV", ZPAV's Warsaw address and phone). The regulation lives at olis.pl/terms_oliw. The subdomain bestsellery.zpav.pl cited by older secondary sources is dead (404 on every path). ALBUM CATEGORIES: the album threshold depends on genre category, and I have reported the "muzyka rozrywkowa" row (pop, rock, metal, rap, hip-hop, dance, K-pop) as the headline because that is the band a mainstream/Afrobeats artist falls into. The other current bands are muzyka poważna/jazz — Gold 5 000, Platinum 10 000, 2x Platinum 20 000, 3x Platinum 30 000, Diamond 50 000, 2x Diamond 100 000, 3x Diamond 150 000; and muzyka filmowa (soundtrack) — 10 000 / 20 000 / 40 000 / 60 000 / 100 000 / 200 000 / 300 000. ELIGIBILITY: an album must have at least 6 different tracks or run at least 25 minutes; a single must be digital, carry identifying digital codes, and plays count only at 30 seconds or more. Singles qualify only if released after 1 January 2015 ("Do wyróżnień kwalifikowane są single, których premiera ... odbyła się po 1 stycznia 2015 roku"), with a discretionary exemption from the ZPAV board. AWARDS ARE APPLICATION-BASED, not automatic: they are granted "na wniosek wydawcy, dystrybutora, producenta lub artysty" — so absence of a Polish plaque never implies the threshold was not met. This is a change from the old regulation, which granted them monthly from ZPAV's own data "bez potrzeby przesyłania wniosków". Premium products are excluded.
countries.sourceQuote: ALBUMY AUDIO (sztuki) — Muzyka rozrywkowa / Muzyka poważna-jazz / Muzyka filmowa: Złota Płyta 15 000 | 5 000 | 10 000; Platynowa Płyta 30 000 | 10 000 | 20 000; Podwójna Platynowa Płyta 60 000 | 20 000 | 40 000; Potrójna Platynowa Płyta 90 000 | 30 000 | 60 000; Diamentowa Płyta 150 000 | 50 000 | 100 000; Podwójna Diamentowa Płyta 300 000 | 100 000 | 200 000; Potrójna Diamentowa Płyta 450 000 | 150 000 | 300 000. — SINGLE AUDIO, Sprzedaż cyfrowa (PLN): Złota Płyta 125 000 zł; Platynowa Płyta 250 000 zł; Podwójna Platynowa Płyta 500 000 zł; Potrójna Platynowa Płyta 750 000 zł; Diamentowa Płyta 1 000 000 zł; Podwójna Diamentowa Płyta 2 000 000 zł; Potrójna Diamentowa Płyta 3 000 000 zł. — "Dla sprzedaży cyfrowej albumów przyjmuje się, że sprzedaż jednego albumu jest równoznaczna z uzyskaniem przychodu 35 zł". — "Niniejszy Regulamin obowiązuje od 1 stycznia 2025." — Superseded table (do końca 2024): "rozrywka - rep. zagraniczny 10 000 / 20 000 / 100 000", "rozrywka - rep. krajowy 15 000 / 30 000 / 150 000", "SINGLE CYFROWE (ilość / wysokość przychodu) 25 000 / 50 000 zł — 50 000 / 100 000 zł — 250 000 / 500 000 zł".

countries.body: IFPI Austria (Verband der Österreichischen Musikwirtschaft)
countries.unitDefinition: Sales plus streaming equivalents ("Verkaufs- bzw. Nutzungszahlen"). A paid download counts the same as a physical sale: "Entgeltliche Downloads eines Einzeltitels bzw. Albums gelten – ebenso wie verkaufte physische Tonträger – als 1 Verkaufseinheit." Sets count once ("bei Sets wird die Anzahl der Sets ... gezählt"). SINGLES/TRACKS convert at TWO rates, and Austria is unusual in counting ad-funded free streams: "171 Premium-Streams bzw. 533 „Free-Streams" eines Einzeltitels entsprechen 1 Verkaufseinheit (d.h. Faktor 171:1 bei Premium-Streams bzw. Faktor 533:1 bei „Free-Streams")" — minimum 30 seconds, official content only, user-generated content excluded. This applies to album tracks as well as released singles. ALBUMS use the "englisches Modell" and free streams do NOT count ("Zur Erinnerung: Free-Streams zählen nicht für die Album-Prämierung!"): at least 6 tracks must be streamed to count as an album, at most 12 tracks count, the two most-streamed tracks are removed and the average of the remaining 4-10 is substituted back for them, and the total is divided by 1710 — "Die Summe der Streams, die auf alle für das Album zählenden Tracks entfallen, wird durch den Faktor 1710 dividiert." Only domestic (Austrian) consumption counts, and at least half of the physical units required must come through traditional retail outlets.
countries.multiplierRule: NOT DEFINED BY THE BODY. The Richtlinien set minimum quantities for Gold and Platin only and contain no formula for multiple awards. However, IFPI Austria's own Gold & Platin database does issue and display multiples in the form "N-fach PLATIN" — entries visible in it on the date of checking include "2-fach PLATIN" (sombr, Back To Friends) and "4-fach PLATIN" (Coldplay, Yellow). So multiples demonstrably exist and are labelled off the Platin tier, but the arithmetic (whether N-fach Platin is literally N x 30 000 for a single / N x 15 000 for an album) is nowhere stated in the body's published rules. Do not assert the multiplication factor as sourced — treat N-fach Platin as an award name IFPI Austria uses, with the underlying quantity unstated. Note also that Austria has no intermediate odd-Gold rung: unlike Germany there is no "3-fach Gold" in the database.
countries.diamondRule: NO DIAMOND TIER. Austria does not award Diamond at all. The Richtlinien recognise exactly two levels throughout — "Die Prämierungen Gold und Platin" — with no Diamant/Diamond row in either the album/single table or the video table, and the public Gold & Platin database shows only GOLD, PLATIN and N-fach PLATIN statuses. Any Austrian 'Diamond' claim is therefore not an IFPI Austria award. Very high sellers are expressed as high multiples of Platin instead.
countries.changedSince2015: The two threshold VALUES (album 7 500 / 15 000, single 15 000 / 30 000) are stated without any release-date banding beyond the guidelines' own scope, and IFPI Austria publishes no previous values, so there is no evidence at the body of the numbers themselves moving. What HAS moved, and is dated by the body, is what counts toward them — clause 12: "Diese Richtlinien gelten für alle Tonträgern bzw. Bildtonträger, die ab dem 1.1.2013 erstmals in Österreich veröffentlicht worden sind. Für das Erreichen der Prämierungsgrenzen werden bei Singles für Veröffentlichungen ab dem 1.1.2015 auch Premium-Streams und ab dem 1.7.2023 zusätzlich auch „Free Streams" mitgezählt. Bei Alben werden Premium-Streams für Veröffentlichungen ab dem 1.1.2017 berücksichtigt." So: singles gained premium streams for releases from 1.1.2015 and ad-funded free streams for releases from 1.7.2023; albums gained premium streams for releases from 1.1.2017. The free-stream addition of 1 July 2023 is the material change inside the 2018-2026 window and makes an Austrian single plaque meaningfully easier to reach for releases from that date. Note these gates key off the RELEASE date, not the award date, so a single first released before 1.7.2023 never gets free streams counted no matter when it is certified. The document itself is current — it is dated "Wien, im April 2025" despite sitting on a 2018 upload path.
countries.notes: CONFIRMED TWICE ON THE BODY'S OWN SITE: the numbers appear both in the linked PDF rulebook and directly on IFPI Austria's awards page at https://ifpi.at/auszeichnungen/, which states "Gold wird verliehen für (VÖ ab dem 1.1.2013) 7.500 verkaufte Alben, 15.000 verkaufte Singles" and "Platin wird verliehen für 15.000 verkaufte Alben, 30.000 verkaufte Singles". Note https://ifpi.at/gold-platin/ 301-redirects to the homepage; /auszeichnungen/ is the live awards page. OTHER CATEGORIES: video carries its own table — Musikvideo Gold 5 000 / Platin 10 000, Special Interest Gold 10 000 / Platin 20 000 — and a video award can be granted in addition to an audio award even when the same video units already counted toward the audio one. ELIGIBILITY: a release must satisfy Austria Top 40 chart eligibility rules to be certifiable at all, and multi-artist compilations are barred where more than half the tracks were previously released. Combination rules are looser than Germany's: albums merge at 50% track overlap (Germany requires 70%); singles merge on the same A-side regardless of version. Only domestic streams/sales count, and exports and parallel-export deliveries are excluded.
countries.sourceQuote: "Die Prämierungen Gold und Platin dürfen für veröffentlichte Alben und Singles in allen handelsüblichen physischen und digitalen Tonträger-Formaten verliehen werden, wenn mindestens folgende Verkaufs- bzw. Nutzungszahlen im Inland erreicht werden. Format / Gold / Platin — Album (Longplay) 7.500 / 15.000; Singles 15.000 / 30.000" ... "Repertoire / Gold / Platin — Musikvideo 5.000 / 10.000; Special Interest 10.000 / 20.000" ... "171 Premium-Streams bzw. 533 „Free-Streams" eines Einzeltitels entsprechen 1 Verkaufseinheit (d.h. Faktor 171:1 bei Premium-Streams bzw. Faktor 533:1 bei „Free-Streams")" ... "Die Summe der Streams, die auf alle für das Album zählenden Tracks entfallen, wird durch den Faktor 1710 dividiert." ... "Wien, im April 2025"

countries.body: IFPI Greece
countries.unitDefinition: NOT PUBLISHED. IFPI Greece states nowhere on its site whether certifications are based on pure sales or on sales plus streaming equivalents, and gives no conversion ratio. Its Digital Singles charts are plainly streaming-driven and carry certification codes, which implies streams count toward at least the digital-single awards, but the body never says so and never states a ratio — so nothing here can be reported as sourced.
countries.multiplierRule: NOT PUBLISHED as a rule, though multiples demonstrably exist: IFPI Greece's own Digital Singles Chart carries an "Award" column whose codes include G, P, 2P, 3P and D (e.g. a 3P and a D appear in the Local chart for week 35/2026). So the body does award 2x and 3x Platinum and a Diamond, but it publishes no threshold behind any of those codes and no statement that N-P equals N times the Platinum figure. The chart's own legend ("επεξήγηση συμβόλων") explains only the movement codes RE, NE, UP and DOWN — it does not decode the award column at all.
countries.diamondRule: Diamond is awarded — a "D" appears in the award column of IFPI Greece's own Digital Singles charts — but whether it is a distinct threshold or a multiple of Platinum is NOT PUBLISHED, and no number is attached to it anywhere on the body's site.
countries.changedSince2015: NOT PUBLISHED. IFPI Greece publishes no current thresholds and therefore no threshold history, no change dates and no previous values. Widely repeated figures for Greece (e.g. album gold at 6 000 and platinum at 12 000, dated to a 2008 or 2009 reduction) trace to Wikipedia, press articles and chart blogs, NOT to IFPI Greece, and under the house rule none of them can be carried over. I have deliberately reported null rather than repeat them. The one thing the body's own pages do show is that certification codes were being printed on its digital singles charts through 2026, so the scheme is live — but its terms are unstated.
countries.notes: THE SITE IS FULLY REACHABLE — this is not a blocking or availability problem, it is a publication gap. I enumerated every page on ifpi.gr and read them: index.html, structure_el.html, mission_el.html, resources_el.html, resources_en.html, links_el.html, news_el.html, isrc_el.html, history1_el.html, charts_el.html, charts_en.html, digital_el.html, digital_iel.html, airplay_el.html, terms_el.htm. None states a certification threshold. The only PDFs the entire site links are two ISRC guides (ISRCfaqGR.pdf, ISRCGuideGR.pdf), neither about certifications. There is no rules, regulation, awards or certifications page, linked or unlinked — I also probed awards_el.html, certifications_el.html, gold_el.html, platinum_el.html, rules_el.html, regulations_el.html, sitemap.xml and robots.txt, all 404. The site has no search facility. The terms page is served in a broken legacy encoding (mojibake) but is a website terms-of-use notice, copyright-dated 2018, with no certification content. PRACTICAL CONSEQUENCE FOR PRICING: Greek plaques can be verified as awarded — the award codes sit on IFPI Greece's own weekly charts against a specific ISRC, which is good provenance for the FACT of a certification — but they cannot be priced in units, because the body publishes no unit value for G, P, 2P, 3P or D. Any Greek unit figure on the site today came from a secondary source and should be treated as unsourced.
countries.sourceQuote: No threshold wording exists to quote. The closest the body comes to publishing anything about certifications is the unexplained "Award" column header on its Official IFPI Charts Digital Singles Chart, whose values are bare codes ("G", "P", "2P", "3P", "D"), accompanied by a legend that decodes only movement: "επεξήγηση συμβόλων — RE: επανείσοδος, NE: νέα είσοδος".
countries.unreadableReason: IFPI Greece's site is fully reachable and was read in full — it simply does not publish its certification thresholds. Every page on ifpi.gr was fetched and searched (all 15 pages reachable from the navigation, in both Greek and English); none contains a Gold, Platinum or Diamond threshold, a streaming conversion ratio, or a certification rulebook. The site links only two PDFs and both concern ISRC codes. No certifications/rules page exists at any probed path (all 404) and there is no sitemap. The body awards certifications and prints the resulting codes (G/P/2P/3P/D) in the Award column of its own Digital Singles charts, but publishes no numeric value behind any code and no legend decoding that column. So the thresholds are null for want of publication by the body, not for want of access.

countries.body: BVMI (Bundesverband Musikindustrie e.V.)
countries.unitDefinition: Sales plus streaming equivalents, in "Einheiten". BVMI states the stream equivalence inline with the numbers: Single Gold is "300.000 Einheiten (dies entspricht 60.000.000 Premium-Streams)" — i.e. 200 premium streams = 1 single unit. SINGLES: premium streams over 30 seconds count at 100:1 up to 5 April 2018 and at 200:1 from 6 April 2018, and ad-funded free streams over 30 seconds count from 30 December 2021 at 1320:1 — "Premium-Streamings über 30 Sekunden werden für den Zeitraum bis zum 5. April 2018 mit einem Faktor von 100:1 und ab dem 6. April 2018 mit einem Faktor von 200:1 bei den Singles berücksichtigt. Free-Streamings über 30 Sekunden werden ab dem 30. Dezember 2021 mit einem Faktor von 1320:1 bei den Singles berücksichtigt." ALBUMS: only premium streams count, only from the 12 most-played tracks, at 1000:1 up to 5 April 2018 and 2000:1 from 6 April 2018 — "Die so ermittelten Premium-Streamings über 30 Sekunden werden bis zum 5. April 2018 mit einem Faktor von 1000:1 und ab dem 6. April 2018 mit einem Faktor von 2000:1 bei den Alben berücksichtigt." The top-track discount changed mid-scheme: for streams up to 7 Dec 2023 the two most-played tracks were replaced by the average of the next ten; for streams from 8 Dec 2023 "Der meistgespielte Track eines Albums wird mit 70 Prozent der erreichten Streams berücksichtigt, die folgenden 11 Tracks werden vollständig gewertet." Streaming counts irrespective of release date (albums since 29 Jan 2016, singles likewise). Only domestic German sales settled with GEMA count; free promo copies are excluded.
countries.multiplierRule: Explicitly defined, and it is NOT a simple N-times-Gold ladder — BVMI skips the even Gold multiples because they collide with Platinum: "Die Abstufungen der Auszeichnungen erfolgt bei Mehrfach-Erreichung immer nach dem Muster: 1fach Gold, 1fach Platin, 3fach Gold, 2fach Platin, 5fach Gold, 3fach Platin, etc. Es werden keine Auszeichnungen für 2fach Gold, 4fach Gold, etc. vergeben, da diese den erforderlichen Mindestmengen der Platinverkäufe entsprechen." So N-fach Platin is literally N x the Platin threshold, and odd Gold multiples fill the half-steps between (3x Gold = 3 x the Gold figure = 1.5 x Platin). Since Platin is exactly 2x Gold in every current band, the ladder is internally consistent. A German award of 19x would be 19x the applicable Platin figure. There is no stated ceiling on Platin multiples.
countries.diamondRule: Diamond is a DISTINCT threshold, not a multiple of Platinum, and it is capped at one award. Albums 750 000 units and singles 1 500 000 units — for post-30.06.2023 albums that happens to be 5x Platin, but for albums released 2003-2023 (Platin 200 000) it is 3.75x Platin, so the ratio is not fixed and Diamond cannot be derived from Platin. Two hard restrictions: it applies ONLY to products first released from 1 January 2013 ("*gilt nur für Produkte mit Erst-VÖ ab 01.01.2013"), and it is awarded once only — "Die DIAMOND-Auszeichnung wird nur einmalig vergeben" — so there is no 2x Diamond in Germany. Diamond also exists only in the main MUSIKPRODUKTE category, not in the video or genre categories.
countries.changedSince2015: YES for albums, and the change is keyed to RELEASE date rather than award date, which matters directly for pricing 2018-2026 plaques. BVMI publishes the full banded history in its current rulebook: albums first released from 30.06.2023 need Gold 75 000 / Platin 150 000; albums first released 01.01.2003-29.06.2023 need Gold 100 000 / Platin 200 000; 25.09.1999-31.12.2002 need 150 000 / 300 000; up to 24.09.1999 need 250 000 / 500 000. So the album thresholds were cut by 25% effective 30 June 2023 — but ONLY for albums released on or after that date. An album first released in, say, 2019 or 2022 still requires 100 000 for Gold today and forever; it does not benefit from the reduction. SINGLES have NOT changed: the current rulebook lists a single un-banded set ("Alle Single-Produkte") of Gold 300 000 / Platin 600 000 applying regardless of release date, with no historical bands published. What changed for singles is the stream conversion, not the target: premium factor 100:1 to 200:1 on 6 April 2018 (a halving of stream value, i.e. a tightening), free streams added at 1320:1 on 30 December 2021 (a loosening), album premium factor 1000:1 to 2000:1 on 6 April 2018, streaming first admitted for albums on 29 January 2016, and the album top-track discount reworked on 8 December 2023. The rulebook in force is Version 3.0, "Stand: 15. Dezember 2023". BVMI's earlier published versions (2.3, 2.5, 2.6) have been removed from the site and now 404, so no earlier single figures can be sourced at the body.
countries.notes: CONFIRMED TWICE ON THE BODY'S OWN SITE: every figure above appears both in the Version 3.0 rulebook PDF and on BVMI's own awards page at https://www.musikindustrie.de/wie-musik-zur-karriere-werden-kann/markt-bestseller/gold-/platin-und-diamond-auszeichnung. CAUTION ON THE PDF: a naive text-summariser reading this PDF returned album Gold 100 000 / Platinum 500 000 / Diamond 1 000 000 and a "1,500 streams = 1 unit" ratio — all four wrong. Those numbers are a hallucination from the binary and match nothing in the document; the figures reported here were taken from the extracted text of the tables in clause 1.4. OTHER CATEGORIES: the album/single figures above cover MUSIKPRODUKTE, KIDS, COMEDY and AUDIO BOOK. Videos have their own much lower table (Gold 25 000 / Platin 50 000, and only for products first released after 1 January 2002 — earlier videos cannot be certified at all). KLASSIK and JAZZ run on separate thresholds set out in clauses 2.3 and 2.4 and are NOT covered by the figures above. COMBINATION RULE: formats merge into one certification where content matches at least 70% of tracks under the same title and artist; multi-artist compilations are barred where most tracks were previously released. Indexed (BzKJ youth-protection listed) titles are stripped out of the count retroactively and the award status adjusted. Since December 2023 GfK Entertainment can supply the proof directly, in which case no auditor certificate is needed.
countries.sourceQuote: "a) Alle Album-Produkte mit Erst-VÖ ab 30.06.2023 — Album Gold 75.000 Einheiten, Album Platin 150.000 Einheiten. Alle Single-Produkte — Single Gold 300.000 Einheiten (dies entspricht 60.000.000 Premium-Streams), Single Platin 600.000 Einheiten (dies entspricht 120.000.000 Premium Streams). b) Alle Album-Produkte mit Erst-VÖ ab 01.01.2003 bis 29.06.2023 — Album Gold 100.000 Einheiten, Album Platin 200.000 Einheiten. c) Alle Album-Produkte mit Erst-VÖ ab 25.09.1999 bis 31.12.2002 — Album Gold 150.000 Einheiten, Album Platin 300.000 Einheiten. d) Alle Album-Produkte mit Erst-VÖ bis 24.09.1999 — Album Gold 250.000 Einheiten, Album Platin 500.000 Einheiten." ... "Die erforderlichen Mindestmengen für DIAMOND ... sind*: Alben 750.000 Einheiten, Singles 1.500.000 Einheiten (entspricht 300.000.000 Premium Streams). *gilt nur für Produkte mit Erst-VÖ ab 01.01.2013" ... "RICHTLINIEN FÜR GOLD/PLATIN/DIAMOND-MELDUNGEN (Version 3.0), Stand: 15. Dezember 2023"

countries.body: BRMA — Belgian Recorded Music Association (renamed from BEA in 2022); the gold/platinum roster is published by Ultratop on BRMA's behalf
countries.unreadableReason: Two-part failure. (1) The certifying body's own site, brma.be, publishes NO certification criteria: I fetched https://www.brma.be/ and enumerated its full sitemap (https://www.brma.be/sitemap.xml) — it contains only /en/home, /en/contact and news-blog posts. There is no thresholds, awards or criteria page anywhere on it.
