Loading it in a real Chrome tab stalls on 'Performing security verification' with a 'Verify you are human' Turnstile checkbox after 30+ seconds of waiting. Completing a bot-detection challenge is not something I will do, so the value cannot be confirmed at the body. NO number is reported rather than carrying one over from Wikipedia or a chart blog.
countries.unitDefinition: Not established — the body's criteria page could not be read.
countries.multiplierRule: Not established — the body's criteria page could not be read.
countries.diamondRule: Not established. Ultratop's roster is branded 'Goud & Platina', which hints there may be no Diamond tier, but that is an inference from a page title I could not open and is NOT confirmed at the body.
countries.changedSince2015: Unknown — not verifiable at the body. Belgium is widely reported to use split domestic/international thresholds and to have moved them, but none of that could be confirmed at BRMA or Ultratop, so nothing is asserted.
countries.notes: IMPORTANT: silverExists=false here is a schema-forced default, NOT a verified finding — treat it as unverified along with everything else for BE. This is the highest-value gap in the batch (5 plaques). Two routes that would close it without breaching the house rule: (a) Paul opens https://www.ultratop.be/nl/info_goud_platina.asp (or the French twin https://www.ultratop.be/fr/info_or_platine.asp) in his own browser, clears the Cloudflare check himself and pastes the text; (b) email BRMA at info@brma.be (Lenneke Marelaan 8, 1932 Sint-Stevens-Woluwe) for the current award criteria in writing. Also note Belgium's roster splits Flanders/Wallonia, so a 'Belgian' plaque may be region-scoped — worth checking when the numbers do land.

countries.body: IFPI Norge AS
countries.unitDefinition: Sales + streaming, combined, but the unit is defined DIFFERENTLY for albums and singles — this is the trap in Norway's numbers. Albums: 'Omregningsfaktor: 1000 streams = 1 salg; 1 nedlastning/fysisk salg = 1 salg' (1,000 streams = 1 sale; 1 download/physical sale = 1 sale). Singles: 'Omregningsfaktor: 1 stream = 1 salg; 1 nedlastning/fysisk salg = 100 salg' (1 stream = 1 sale; 1 download/physical sale = 100 sales). So the single figures are counted in RAW STREAMS, which is why Gold is 3,000,000 and not 30,000 — 3,000,000 streams is the same as 30,000 download-equivalents. Scope is 'Fysisk, digital og streaming' in Norway.
countries.multiplierRule: The body publishes NO written multiplier rule. Its own trophy register (https://ifpi.no/trofe/trofeoversikt/) carries a 'Nivå' (level) column whose values are 1x, 2x, 3x, 4x, 9x alongside the Platina marker — i.e. awards are expressed as N×, consistent with N times the Platinum threshold — but IFPI Norge never states that in prose, so treat 'Nx = N × 20,000 album units / N × 6,000,000 single streams' as inferred-from-their-register, not quoted.
countries.diamondRule: No Diamond tier. Both criteria pages say only 'IFPI Norge utsteder de offisielle gull og platina-troféene' — gold and platinum trophies. Diamond appears nowhere on the site, and the register's legend has exactly two symbols: '= Gull' and '= Platina'.
countries.changedSince2015: Not stated by the body — and that is a finding, not a gap I glossed over. IFPI Norge publishes the current criteria only, with no effective date and no history table. I searched its own page list (page-sitemap.xml, 29 pages) and its WordPress search index for 'kriterier', 'grense', 'gull' and 'endring'; the only hits are the criteria pages themselves and unrelated interview posts. So: no change history is published, and I am NOT carrying one over from elsewhere. Practical consequence for plaques spanning 2018-2026 — the site gives no way to tell whether a 2018 plaque was earned against these same numbers.
countries.notes: The identical figures appear on TWO of the body's own pages, which is a useful cross-check: https://ifpi.no/trofe/ ('Fysisk, digital og streaming') and https://ifpi.no/vilkar/ ('Antall salg – Streaming, fysisk og nedlastning'). Third category: Musikk-DVD, at Gull 5.000 / Platina 10.000, 'Omregningsfaktor: 1 fysisk salg / nedlasting = 1 enhet' (https://ifpi.no/trofe/soknadsskjema/musikk-dvd/). Awards are label-applied and approved on a rolling basis ('godkjenning skjer fortløpende'), so absence from the register means no application was made, not that a release fell short.
countries.sourceQuote: ALBUM Gull 10.000 Platina 20.000 /// Omregningsfaktor: 1000 streams = 1 salg, 1 nedlastning/fysisk salg = 1 salg | SINGEL Gull 3.000.000 Platina 6.000.000 /// Omregningsfaktor: 1 stream = 1 salg, 1 nedlastning/fysisk salg = 100 salg

countries.body: MAHASZ — Magyar Hangfelvétel-kiadók Szövetsége (the Hungarian group of IFPI)
countries.unitDefinition: Sales + streaming equivalents, in 'értékesítési egység' (sales units), and the conversion ratios differ by category. Albums: physical album 1:1, digital album 1:1, single track download 1:25, premium stream 1:3700, ad-funded stream 1:12275. Singles: physical single 1:1, full digital release 1:1, single track download 1:1, premium stream 1:148, ad-funded stream 1:491. countries.multiplierRule: Literally N times the Platinum threshold, and MAHASZ states it in those words for both categories: 'A platina értékesítési egységek egész számú többszörösei után dupla, tripla, stb. platina minősítés jár' — whole-number multiples of the platinum sales units earn double, triple, etc. platinum. So for a current single, 5x Platinum = 50,000 units.
countries.diamondRule: Not currently awarded. Gyémánt (Diamond) was a real tier historically — the body's own history table gives it as 400,000 for albums up to 1992-06-12 and 200,000 from 1992-06-12 — but the column reads '-' from 1997-12-03 onward and there is no Diamond row in either current table. The intro also frames Silver and Diamond as things other countries do: 'egyes országokban még ezüst, illetve gyémánt'.
countries.changedSince2015: YES, and this one bites directly on 2018-2026 plaques — SINGLES moved twice inside the window. From the body's own history page (https://slagerlistak.hu/arany-es-platinalemezek/a-dijak-tortenete): singles were Arany 1,500 / Platina 3,000 from 2009-10-01; Arany 2,000 / Platina 4,000 from 2018-01-01; and Arany 5,000 / Platina 10,000 only from 2026-02-10. ALBUMS have not moved since 2012-12-14 (2,000 / 4,000). So a Hungarian single plaque awarded between Jan 2018 and Feb 2026 was earned at 2,000 (Gold) / 4,000 (Platinum) — do NOT price those against the current 5,000/10,000.
countries.notes: Provenance: slagerlistak.hu is MAHASZ's own official charts site — mahasz.hu/arany_platina links straight into it and the page footer reads 'Magyar Hangfelvétel-kiadók Szövetsége ... (Az IFPI magyar csoportja)'. Two extra wrinkles: (1) for releases published before 2012-12-14 a separate conversion ladder applies (1:50 up to 1992-06-12, down through 1:25, 1:12.5, 1:7.5, 1:5, 1:3.75, 1:2.5, to 1:1 from 2012-12-14) because the old thresholds were in physical copies; (2) streaming ratios are uniform regardless of release date. MAHASZ publishes a downloadable Excel calculator labels use to file a claim, and certification is claim-driven, so absence from the database is not evidence of falling short. Categories are ALBUM and KISLEMEZ (single) only — no EP or video tier in the current rules.
countries.sourceQuote: Az ALBUM arany minősítés eléréséhez egységesen (műfajtól, eredettől függetlenül) 2000, a platina minősítéshez 4000 egységnyi értékesítés szükséges … A KISLEMEZ arany minősítés eléréséhez egységesen 5000, a platina minősítéshez 10000 egységnyi értékesítés szükséges

countries.body: AMPROFON — Asociación Mexicana de Productores de Fonogramas y Videogramas
countries.unitDefinition: Split by category, and AMPROFON does NOT publish a stream-to-unit ratio. Albums are 'Niveles medidos en unidades equivalentes' (levels measured in equivalent units) — the PDF says physical album sales may be topped up with premium physical editions, full digital album and pre-loaded album sales, and, for releases from 2020-11-01, with video streams of the album's tracks; it never states how many streams make a unit. Singles are 'Niveles medidos en audio streams' — the thresholds ARE raw audio-stream counts, not converted units, which is why Gold is 22,000,000. UGC video is excluded in both categories.
countries.multiplierRule: Not defined anywhere in the criteria PDF. What AMPROFON's own live register does show is that levels STACK cumulatively rather than reading as a single 'Nx Platinum': its certification table has a 'NIVEL DE CERTIFICACIÓN' column carrying entries like 'DIAMANTE & PLATINO & ORO' with levels '1 & 3 & 1', and 'DIAMANTE & PLATINO' with '2 & 3'. Read a Mexican award as an accumulated stack (e.g. 1 Diamond + 3 Platinum + 1 Gold), not as a simple multiple — this is the observed behaviour of their register at https://amprofon.com.mx/es/pages/certificaciones.php, not a quoted rule.
countries.diamondRule: Diamond is a DISTINCT published threshold with its own number, not a shorthand for N× Platinum — though arithmetically it lands at exactly 5× Platinum in both categories (albums 700,000 vs 140,000; singles 220,000,000 vs 44,000,000). It has its own history too: for albums released 2003-07-01 to 2007-12-31 Diamond was 'N/A', and a separate legacy Diamond of 500,000 (releases 2000-2007) / 1,000,000 (pre-2000) is listed.
countries.changedSince2015: YES — a major reset on 2020-11-01, squarely inside the 2018-2026 plaque window, and the thresholds key off RELEASE date, not award date. Albums: 70,000 / 140,000 / 700,000 for releases from 2020-11-01; previously 30,000 / 60,000 / 300,000 for releases 2009-07-01 to 2020-10-31. Singles: 22,000,000 / 44,000,000 / 220,000,000 for releases from 2020-11-01; previously 9,300,000 / 18,600,000 / 93,000,000 for releases before 2020-10-31. Also relevant: from 2015-02-18 music-video certification may combine physical DVD and digital LFV units, and video streams were folded into album and single criteria in 2020.
countries.notes: CRITICAL for pricing: AMPROFON's thresholds are indexed to the RELEASE date of the recording, not the date the plaque was issued. A Mexican plaque awarded in 2024 for a song released in 2019 was earned at 9,300,000 audio streams for Gold, not 22,000,000 — check each title's release date before applying a number. Fourth category exists: physical music video / long-format video (DVD), Oro 10,000 / Platino 20,000 / Diamante 100,000 for releases from 2014-02-19 (Diamond 'N/A' with no release-date restriction before that). Single-track certification may aggregate different-language, different-genre, acoustic and live versions of the same song. The register is label-request-driven (a label 'envía a AMPROFON la solicitud'), so absence is not evidence of falling short. Criteria PDF is linked from https://amprofon.com.mx/es/pages/certificaciones.php as 'Antecedentes y Criterios de Certificaciones'.
countries.sourceQuote: CRITERIOS PARA LA CERTIFICACION DE VENTAS DE ÁLBUMES — Niveles medidos en unidades equivalentes. Lanzamientos a partir del 1ro de noviembre de 2020: Disco de Oro: 70,000; Disco de Platino: 140,000; Disco de Diamante: 700,000 … CRITERIOS PARA LA CERTIFICACION DE SINGLE TRACKS … Niveles medidos en audio streams: Disco de Oro: 22,000,000; Disco de Platino: 44,000,000; Disco de Diamante: 220,000,000

countries.body: PRO MÚSICA (Pro Música Colombia) — IFPI-affiliated body covering Colombia, Ecuador and Peru
countries.unreadableReason: The site itself is fully readable — the body simply does not publish its unit thresholds anywhere. This is a 'does not publish', not a 'could not reach'. countries.unitDefinition: Not published. The body says only that it awards for 'la música más vendida en formatos físicos y digitales' — most-sold music in physical and digital formats. No streaming ratio, no unit definition, no numbers.
countries.multiplierRule: Not published, and its register gives no sign of one: the certifications PDF records a single flat tier per row (ORO / PLATINO / DIAMANTE) with no multiplier or level column — unlike Mexico's register, which does carry stacked levels. So there is no evidence Pro Música issues multi-platinum awards at all, but that is an observation about the register's shape, not a stated rule.
countries.diamondRule: Diamante IS awarded and is named by the body as one of its three tiers, and it appears throughout the register (e.g. album and single rows dated 2024). But no threshold value is published, so whether it is a distinct number or a multiple of Platino is unknown.
countries.changedSince2015: Not published. The body states no thresholds at all, therefore no history and no change dates. Nothing can be said about whether the basis for a 2018 plaque differs from a 2026 one.
countries.notes: Both CO plaques are affected. disputed.corrections:
The numbers in the claim are, I believe, operationally CORRECT -- but the claim is mis-sourced on one of them, and the cited page will actively contradict anyone who checks it. That is why agrees=false, not because 10,000,000 is wrong.

1) THE REAL PROBLEM -- album Diamond. The claim says album Diamond = 10,000,000 and cites https://www.riaa.com/gold-platinum/about-awards/. That page's Full-Length Album Award, Shortform Album/EP Award and Multi-Disc Set tables all print "Diamond | 2,000,000 units". The page contradicts itself: its own top-level Certification Levels table says Diamond = 10,000,000 units, and every RIAA/GR&F audit PDF (2016, 2022, 2023) says "Diamond - 10,000,000 Units" for the Album Award. 10,000,000 is the operative figure -- RIAA awards album Diamond at 10 million, and 2,000,000 is a stale/erroneous cell on the marketing page (it looks like the old "Multi-Platinum 2,000,000" row mislabelled "Diamond" in all three album tables). ACTION: keep 10,000,000, but re-cite album Diamond to https://www.riaa.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/09/ALBUM-AWARD-RIAA-AND-GRF-CERTIFICATION-AUDIT-REQUIREMENTS52.pdf (and/or the Certification Levels table on the same page), and leave a note in the data so a future checker does not "correct" album Diamond down to 2,000,000 off the about-awards table. Do not publish 2,000,000.

2) Mis-attributed quote in the multiplier rule. The claim says "The Digital Single Award PDF adds that even above Diamond the count continues '(increments of 1,000,000 thereafter)'." In the CURRENT (2023/09) single PDF that parenthetical sits on the Platinum line only -- "Platinum - 1,000,000 Units (increments of 1,000,000 thereafter)" -- and the Diamond line carries no parenthetical at all. Only the older 2016 PDF puts "(increments of 1,000,000 thereafter)" on the Diamond line. Above-Diamond continuation is still supported, but by a different sentence: the about-awards Digital Single table's Diamond row says "Recertified at each million unit sales level". Fix the attribution or the multiplier rule quotes a line that is not where the claim says it is.

3) Small wording drifts, worth tightening but not disqualifying on their own:
   - "official label/artist videos" -> RIAA says "official label/company videos".
   - "non-interactive streams excluded" is an inference, not page wording; RIAA only ever specifies on-demand streams.
   - "Recertified at each subsequent million units" is the album/shortform/multi-disc wording; the Digital Single table says "Recertified at each million units" (no "subsequent").
   - Full-Length wording is "Album sales, single sales and on-demand..."; Shortform has the serial comma ("Album sales, single sales, and on-demand..."). If those strings are stored as quotes, store them per-award.

4) Confirmed correct, no change needed: Silver = null for both single and album (RIAA has no Silver tier); single Gold 500,000 / Platinum 1,000,000 / Diamond 10,000,000; album Gold 500,000 / Platinum 1,000,000; the 1,500:10:1 album formula and the 150:1 single formula, correctly kept distinct (no single/album conflation); Multi-Platinum = N x 1,000,000; US-only sales/streams; official videos only.

5) Not an error, but a gap: the same page defines a separate Latin program (Oro 30,000 / Platino 60,000 / Multi-Platino 120,000 in increments of 60,000 / Diamante 600,000) for releases with >50% Spanish-language lyrics. If the dataset carries one US row with the general thresholds, it should say so explicitly, or a Latin-certified title will be scored against the wrong ladder.
